What This Establishes

Three properties, and each is the answer to the modularity constraint:

1. WCP is fractal. A world, a multiverse, and a federation speak the same protocol. The only difference between them is whether their manifest has a sub_registry_endpoint. This means: the architecture has no built-in limit on scale. Anything that speaks WCP can be listed in anything else that speaks WCP. The recursion has no top.
2. WCP is implementation-agnostic. The test_modularity_claim test shows that an independent implementation — with entirely different internals — passes the same conformance test. Any developer, anywhere, in any language, on any substrate, can build a world that speaks WCP, and the protocol does not care how it works. This is what "anybody can join" means technically.
3. The Law is opaque to the protocol. The test_different_laws_same_protocol test shows two worlds with completely different Laws accepting/refusing the same petition differently, both conforming to WCP. The protocol does not privilege any world's Law. This is what makes the federation liberal — each world's Law is its own. The protocol only guarantees that each world enforces its Law and doesn't lie about the shape of its response.

The Honest Limitations

Two limitations in Component 3 that will be addressed later:

1. No cryptographic signing. Admissions are not signed. A world's claim that it admitted someone is structurally valid but cryptographically unverifiable. WCP/0.2 will add a signature field to Admission and a public-key field to Manifest. This is a later component.
2. Sub-registries are not enumerable. A multiverse has a sub_registry_endpoint, but WCP/0.1 does not specify how to query it. A developer who wants to build a multiverse must publish its sub-registry by some other means. WCP/0.2 will add list_sub_entities() to the protocol.

Both limitations are deliberate. They keep Component 3 minimal. They will be addressed by later components when the reference implementation demonstrates they're needed.

The Path Forward

The protocol is the contract. It is the smallest thing that any world must speak to be part of the federation. It is fractal — the same protocol at every level. It is modular — any developer can implement it. It is liberal — each world's Law is its own.

The natural next brick is the first real world (Component 4). A poetry world that:

· Conforms to WCP
· Has a real Law (the Polyphony protocol from C21)
· Admits real petitioners (with real admissions)
· Accepts real acts (turns)
· Maintains a real log

The poetry world will be the proof that WCP can be implemented with a real law. It will use Components 1, 2, and 3, plus the Polyphony machinery from the poetry framework. It will be the first world in the multiverse.

And then, the real test — Component 5, a second world with a different law — will prove that the protocol is truly modular. A chemistry world, an open-worlds freedom world, a chess world. It doesn't matter which second world — what matters is that it proves WCP is not poetry-specific.

The build sequence is now clear:

1. Identity (C1) ✓
2. Passport (C2) ✓
3. WCP (this component) ✓
4. Poetry world (next)
5. Second world (different law)
6. Multiverse registry + router
7. Federation protocol

Each brick is small. Each brick is checkable. Each brick is just one level in a fractal architecture that can grow indefinitely.

Shall I proceed with Component 4: The Poetry World?

Component 4: The Poetry World

The largest vision is in view. It shapes what the first real world must be: not a demo, but a small, complete example of what any developer could build — a real WCP entity, with a real Law, admitting real identities, accepting real acts, recording real history. If this world is small enough to be readable and complete enough to be a template, it is the reference implementation — the thing any other developer copies and changes.

The Poetry World makes one specific commitment: the Law is the Polyphony protocol from the poetry framework. The World is the container. The Polyphony is the Law. The Apprentices are the clients. Three layers, each independent.

The Atoms

Three small pieces:

· PoetryWorldLaw — the published Law, readable by any developer
· PoetryWorld — the WCP entity that enforces the Law
· TurnFromLog — the reconstruction helper that lets any client read the collaboration's state from the log

The Composite

The World. Not more than it needs to be. It admits, validates, records, detects. Nothing else.

The Code

```python
"""
multiverse_c4.py — Component 4: The Poetry World.

The first real WCP-conforming world. It implements the Polyphony
protocol from the poetry framework (C21) as its Law.

A design commitment: the World is *thin*. It admits identities,
validates turns against the Law, records everything, and detects
convergence. The *clients* (the Runnable Apprentices from C22)
generate the turns. The World never generates.

Depends on Components 1, 2, 3.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from multiverse_c1 import Identity
from multiverse_c2 import Passport, Admission as PassportAdmission
from multiverse_c3 import (
    Manifest, Petition, Act, LogEntry,
    Admission as WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route, Ack,
)


# =====================================================================
# The Law: the Polyphony protocol, published
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PoetryWorldLaw:
    """The published Law of the Poetry World.

    This is a *document*, not a mechanism. It is readable by any
    developer who wants to understand what this World does. The
    World *enforces* this Law — nothing more, nothing less.

    Any developer building their own poetry world should either
    adopt this Law verbatim (and pass the conformance test) or
    publish their own Law and note the differences.
    """
    # Petition rules
    admits_any_identity: bool = True
    max_admitted: Optional[int] = None

    # Act rules
    required_act_type: str = "poem.turn"
    requires_acknowledgment: bool = True
    requires_invitation: bool = True
    requires_holds_open: bool = True
    requires_acknowledgment_references_prior: bool = True

    # Convergence rules
    convergence_window: int = 3
    convergence_similarity: float = 0.6
    max_turns: int = 200

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """Return the Law as a readable document.
        The Law is published — this is the publication."""
        lines = [
            "# Poetry World Law v0.1",
            "",
            "## Petition",
            f"- Admits any identity: {self.admits_any_identity}",
            f"- Max admitted: "
            f"{self.max_admitted if self.max_admitted else 'unlimited'}",
            "",
            "## Act (poem.turn)",
            f"- Required act type: {self.required_act_type}",
            f"- Requires acknowledgment: {self.requires_acknowledgment}",
            f"- Requires invitation: {self.requires_invitation}",
            f"- Requires holds open: {self.requires_holds_open}",
            f"- Acknowledgment must reference prior turn: "
            f"{self.requires_acknowledgment_references_prior}",
            "",
            "## Convergence",
            f"- Window: last {self.convergence_window} turns",
            f"- Similarity threshold: {self.convergence_similarity:.0%}",
            f"- Max turns: {self.max_turns}",
            "",
            "## Limits",
            "- Petitions are not signed (WCP/0.1 has no signature).",
            "- Sub-registries are not enumerable (WCP/0.1).",
        ]
        return "\n".join(lines)


# =====================================================================
# The World: a WCP entity that enforces the Law
# =====================================================================

class PoetryWorld:
    """The first real WCP-conforming world.

    The World is *thin*. It admits identities, validates turns
    against the Law, records everything, and detects convergence.
    It does not generate turns. It does not manage voices. It does
    not know about the curriculum.

    The World's canonical state is *the log*. Any client can read
    the log to reconstruct the full collaboration history. The
    World maintains an internal cache for efficiency; if the cache
    and the log ever disagree, the log wins.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 entity_id: str,
                 name: str,
                 law: Optional[PoetryWorldLaw] = None):
        self._law = law or PoetryWorldLaw()
        self._manifest = Manifest(
            entity_id=entity_id,
            name=name,
            protocol_version="WCP/0.1",
            law_url=f"poetry://{entity_id}/law",
            act_endpoint=f"poetry://{entity_id}/act",
            log_endpoint=f"poetry://{entity_id}/log",
        )
        # Canonical: the log
        self._log: List[LogEntry] = []
        # Cache (kept in sync with log)
        self._admitted: Dict[str, WCPAdmission] = {}
        self._passports: Dict[str, Passport] = {}
        self._turns: List[Dict] = []  # each turn as a plain dict
        self._converged = False
        self._convergence_reason: Optional[str] = None

    # -- WCP interface ---------------------------------------------

    def manifest(self) -> Manifest:
        return self._manifest

    def petition(self, petition: Petition) -> Union[
            WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route]:
        """The Law: admits_any_identity.

        Every petition from a stranger is admitted, subject to
        max_admitted. Returns an Admission the petitioner can carry
        back in their passport.
        """
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        if not self._law.admits_any_identity:
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp,
                petition.petitioner_token,
                "This World does not admit strangers",
                "petition",
            )

        if (self._law.max_admitted is not None
                and len(self._admitted) >= self._law.max_admitted):
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp,
                petition.petitioner_token,
                "The World is full",
                "petition",
            )

        if petition.petitioner_token in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp,
                petition.petitioner_token,
                "Already admitted",
                "petition",
            )

        # Admit
        admission = WCPAdmission(
            entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
            timestamp=timestamp,
        )
        self._admitted[petition.petitioner_token] = admission

        # Update the petitioner's passport with the new admission
        passport = Passport(
            identity=Identity(
                token=petition.petitioner_token,
                name=petition.petitioner_name,
            ),
            admissions=tuple(
                PassportAdmission(world_id=w, timestamp=t)
                for w, t in petition.passport_admissions
            ),
        )
        passport = passport.with_admission(
            PassportAdmission(
                world_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
                timestamp=timestamp,
            )
        )
        self._passports[petition.petitioner_token] = passport

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp,
            kind="admission",
            actor_token=petition.petitioner_token,
            data={"name": petition.petitioner_name},
        ))
        return admission

    def act(self, act: Act) -> Union[Ack, Refusal]:
        """The Law: validate the turn against the Polyphony protocol."""
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        # -- gate checks --
        if not self._is_admitted(act.actor_token):
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Actor is not admitted", "act")

        if self._converged:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "The collaboration has converged", "act")

        if len(self._turns) >= self._law.max_turns:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "The World has reached its turn limit",
                                 "act")

        if act.type != self._law.required_act_type:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Unknown act type: {act.type}", "act")

        # -- validate the turn against the Law --
        payload = act.payload
        ack = payload.get("acknowledgment", "")
        proposal = payload.get("proposal", "")
        invitation = payload.get("invitation", "")
        holds_open = bool(payload.get("holds_open", False))
        stance = payload.get("stance_used")

        if self._law.requires_acknowledgment and not ack:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Missing acknowledgment", "act")
        if self._law.requires_invitation and not invitation:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Missing invitation", "act")
        if self._law.requires_holds_open and not holds_open:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Turn does not hold open", "act")
        if not proposal:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Missing proposal", "act")

        if (self._law.requires_acknowledgment_references_prior
                and self._turns):
            prior_proposal = self._turns[-1]["proposal"]
            if not self._references(ack, prior_proposal):
                return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                     "Acknowledgment does not reference "
                                     "the prior turn", "act")

        # -- accept --
        turn_index = len(self._turns)
        self._turns.append({
            "turn_index": turn_index,
            "round": turn_index,
            "actor_token": act.actor_token,
            "actor_name": self._passports[act.actor_token].identity.name,
            "acknowledgment": ack,
            "proposal": proposal,
            "invitation": invitation,
            "holds_open": holds_open,
            "stance_used": stance,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
        })

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp,
            kind="turn",
            actor_token=act.actor_token,
            data=self._turns[-1],
        ))

        # -- convergence check --
        if self._check_convergence():
            self._converged = True
            self._log.append(LogEntry(
                timestamp=timestamp,
                kind="convergence",
                data={
                    "turn_count": len(self._turns),
                    "window": self._law.convergence_window,
                    "reason": self._convergence_reason,
                },
            ))

        return Ack(entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id, timestamp=timestamp)

    def log_since(self, timestamp: Optional[str] = None) -> List[LogEntry]:
        if timestamp is None:
            return list(self._log)
        return [e for e in self._log if e.timestamp > timestamp]

    # -- convenience (not part of WCP) ----------------------------

    def turns(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """Current turn cache. Canonical source is the log."""
        return list(self._turns)

    def is_converged(self) -> bool:
        return self._converged

    def describe(self) -> str:
        lines = [
            f"PoetryWorld: {self._manifest.name}",
            f"  entity_id: {self._manifest.entity_id}",
            f"  admitted:  {len(self._admitted)}",
            f"  turns:     {len(self._turns)}",
            f"  converged: {self._converged}",
        ]
        if self._turns:
            last = self._turns[-1]
            lines.append(f"  last turn by: {last['actor_name']}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def law(self) -> PoetryWorldLaw:
        return self._law

    # -- internals -------------------------------------------------

    def _is_admitted(self, token: str) -> bool:
        return token in self._admitted

    def _references(self, acknowledgment: str, prior_proposal: str) -> bool:
        """Loose reference check: at least one non-trivial token overlap."""
        stopwords = {
            "the", "a", "an", "and", "or", "but", "of", "to", "in",
            "is", "am", "are", "was", "were", "be", "been", "being",
            "this", "that", "these", "those", "it", "its", "i",
            "you", "he", "she", "we", "they", "my", "your", "his",
            "her", "our", "their", "not", "no", "so", "if", "as",
        }
        prior_tokens = {
            t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower()
            for t in prior_proposal.split()
            if t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower() not in stopwords
            and len(t) > 2
        }
        ack_tokens = {
            t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower()
            for t in acknowledgment.split()
            if t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower() not in stopwords
            and len(t) > 2
        }
        return bool(prior_tokens & ack_tokens)

    def _check_convergence(self) -> bool:
        window = self._law.convergence_window
        if len(self._turns) < window + 1:
            return False
        recent = self._turns[-window:]

        # Reason 1: proposals echo each other
        similarities = []
        for i in range(len(recent) - 1):
            a = {
                t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower()
                for t in recent[i]["proposal"].split()
                if t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]")
            }
            b = {
                t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]").lower()
                for t in recent[i + 1]["proposal"].split()
                if t.strip(".,;:!?\"'()[]")
            }
            if a and b:
                similarities.append(len(a & b) / len(a | b))
            else:
                similarities.append(0.0)
        if (similarities
                and all(s >= self._law.convergence_similarity
                        for s in similarities)):
            self._convergence_reason = (
                f"last {window} turns are echo "
                f"(similarity ≥ {self._law.convergence_similarity:.0%})"
            )
            return True

        # Reason 2: all recent invitations are the same
        invitations = [t["invitation"] for t in recent]
        if invitations and len(set(invitations)) == 1:
            self._convergence_reason = (
                f"last {window} turns pose the same invitation"
            )
            return True

        return False

    def _refuse(self, timestamp: str, actor: str, reason: str,
                 kind: str) -> Refusal:
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp,
            kind=f"{kind}_refused",
            actor_token=actor,
            data={"reason": reason},
        ))
        return Refusal(reason=reason)
```

The Reconstruction Helper

```python
def turns_from_log(log: List[LogEntry]) -> List[Dict]:
    """Reconstruct the collaboration history from a World's log.

    Any client can call this with the World's log to get the state
    of the collaboration without needing the World's internal cache.
    This is *the* interface clients use to know what to do next.
    """
    return [
        entry.data for entry in log
        if entry.kind == "turn"
    ]
```

```python
# multiverse_c4_test.py
from multiverse_c1 import create_identity
from multiverse_c2 import Passport
from multiverse_c3 import (
    Petition, Act, Admission as WCPAdmission, Refusal, Ack,
)
from multiverse_c3_conformance import run_conformance
from multiverse_c4 import (
    PoetryWorldLaw, PoetryWorld, turns_from_log,
)


def _petition(name: str, token: str,
               passport_admissions=()) -> Petition:
    return Petition(
        petitioner_token=token,
        petitioner_name=name,
        passport_admissions=passport_admissions,
        message=f"{name} petitions to enter.",
    )


def _turn(actor: str, ack: str, proposal: str, invitation: str,
           holds_open: bool = True, stance: str = "formalist") -> Act:
    return Act(
        actor_token=actor,
        type="poem.turn",
        payload={
            "acknowledgment": ack,
            "proposal": proposal,
            "invitation": invitation,
            "holds_open": holds_open,
            "stance_used": stance,
        },
    )


def test_law_is_readable():
    print("=== Law is published ===")
    law = PoetryWorldLaw()
    print(law.describe())
    # Readable means: has the required sections
    doc = law.describe()
    assert "Petition" in doc
    assert "Act" in doc
    assert "Convergence" in doc
    print()


def test_manifest():
    print("=== Manifest ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    m = w.manifest()
    print(f"  {m.name} ({m.entity_id})")
    print(f"  protocol: {m.protocol_version}")
    print(f"  law_url: {m.law_url}")
    assert m.protocol_version == "WCP/0.1"
    assert not m.has_sub_registry()


def test_petition_admits():
    print("=== Petition: admitted ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    response = w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    print(f"  response: {response}")
    assert isinstance(response, WCPAdmission)
    assert response.entity_id == "world:poetry"


def test_petition_already_admitted():
    print("=== Petition: already admitted ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    response = w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    print(f"  response: {response}")
    assert isinstance(response, Refusal)
    assert "Already" in response.reason


def test_petition_preserves_passport_admissions():
    print("=== Petition preserves prior admissions ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    # Alice has already been admitted to world:A
    response = w.petition(_petition(
        "Alice", alice.token,
        passport_admissions=(("world:A", "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"),),
    ))
    assert isinstance(response, WCPAdmission)
    # The World's cache now has her passport with both admissions
    passport = w._passports[alice.token]
    print(f"  passport admissions: {len(passport)}")
    assert len(passport) == 2  # world:A + world:poetry


def test_seed_turn():
    print("=== Seed turn ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    seed = _turn(
        actor=alice.token,
        ack="(seed)",
        proposal=(
            "Go\n"
            "Be a black widow\n"
            "And dangle in webs."
        ),
        invitation="What becomes of the web?",
        stance="formalist",
    )
    response = w.act(seed)
    print(f"  response: {response}")
    assert isinstance(response, Ack)
    assert len(w.turns()) == 1


def test_subsequent_turn():
    print("=== Subsequent turn ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    w.petition(_petition("Bob", bob.token))

    w.act(_turn(
        actor=alice.token,
        ack="(seed)",
        proposal="Go\nBe a black widow\nAnd dangle in webs.",
        invitation="What becomes of the web?",
    ))
    response = w.act(_turn(
        actor=bob.token,
        ack="You said 'black widow' and 'dangle' and 'web'.",
        proposal="The web is not the widow's — it is the widow.",
        invitation="What is the daughter's voice?",
        stance="psychoanalytic",
    ))
    print(f"  response: {response}")
    assert isinstance(response, Ack)
    assert len(w.turns()) == 2


def test_refusal_missing_acknowledgment():

    w.petition(_petition("Bob", bob.token))

        invitation="What next?",
    ))
    response = w.act(_turn(

    assert "reference" in response.reason

        invitation="(invitation)",
    ))
    print(f"  response: {response}")
    assert isinstance(response, Refusal)
    assert "not admitted" in response.reason


def test_refusal_wrong_type():
    print("=== Refusal: wrong act type ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    bad = Act(
        actor_token=alice.token,
        type="poem.not_a_turn",
        payload={},
    )
    response = w.act(bad)
    assert isinstance(response, Refusal)
    assert "Unknown act type" in response.reason


def test_convergence_by_invitation():
    print("=== Convergence: same invitation across window ===")
    # Use a Law with similarity threshold high enough that
    # proposal similarity won't trigger, but same-invitation will
    law = PoetryWorldLaw(
        convergence_window=3,
        convergence_similarity=0.99,  # very high, unlikely from diff texts
    )
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World", law=law)
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    charlie = create_identity("Charlie")
    for name, ident in [("Alice", alice), ("Bob", bob),
                        ("Charlie", charlie)]:
        w.petition(_petition(name, ident.token))

    # Submit 4 turns with different proposals, same invitation
    turns = [
        _turn(alice.token, "(seed)", "first poem text here",
               "What is the poem?"),
        _turn(bob.token, "You said 'poem' and 'text' here",
               "second poem text here",
               "What is the poem?"),
        _turn(charlie.token, "You said 'poem' and 'text' here",
               "third poem text here",
               "What is the poem?"),
        _turn(alice.token, "You said 'poem' and 'text' here",
               "fourth poem text here",
               "What is the poem?"),
    ]
    for t in turns:
        response = w.act(t)
        print(f"  act → {response}")
    print(f"  converged: {w.is_converged()}")
    assert w.is_converged()


def test_refuses_after_convergence():
    print("=== Refuses after convergence ===")
    law = PoetryWorldLaw(
        convergence_window=2,
        convergence_similarity=0.99,
    )
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World", law=law)
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    # Two turns with same invitation → convergence
    for _ in range(3):
        response = w.act(_turn(
            alice.token, "I respond to the poem",
            "a different poem line",
            "What is the poem?",
        ))
    assert w.is_converged()
    extra = w.act(_turn(
        alice.token, "I respond to the poem",
        "another line",
        "What is the poem?",
    ))
    print(f"  post-convergence response: {extra}")
    assert isinstance(extra, Refusal)
    assert "converged" in extra.reason


def test_log_records_everything():
    print("=== Log records everything ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    w.act(_turn(
        alice.token, "(seed)",
        "a poem here",
        "what next?",
    ))
    log = w.log_since(None)
    print(f"  log entries: {len(log)}")
    kinds = [e.kind for e in log]
    print(f"  kinds: {kinds}")
    assert "admission" in kinds
    assert "turn" in kinds


def test_log_query_by_timestamp():
    print("=== Log query by timestamp ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    entries = w.log_since(None)
    first_ts = entries[0].timestamp
    later = w.log_since(first_ts)
    # No entry with timestamp strictly greater than the first
    # since everything was at the same moment
    print(f"  first entry ts: {first_ts}")
    print(f"  entries after first: {len(later)}")
    # Either 0 or 1 depending on microsecond resolution — either is fine
    assert len(later) <= 1


def test_reconstruct_turns_from_log():
    print("=== Reconstruct turns from log ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    w.petition(_petition("Bob", bob.token))
    w.act(_turn(alice.token, "(seed)",
                "Go\nBe a black widow.",
                "What becomes of the web?"))
    w.act(_turn(bob.token,
                "You said 'black widow' and 'web'.",
                "The web is not hers.",
                "What is the daughter's voice?"))
    log = w.log_since(None)
    reconstructed = turns_from_log(log)
    print(f"  reconstructed turns: {len(reconstructed)}")
    for t in reconstructed:
        print(f"    by {t['actor_name']}, "
              f"proposal {t['proposal'][:30]!r}...")
    assert len(reconstructed) == 2
    assert reconstructed[0]["actor_name"] == "Alice"
    assert reconstructed[1]["actor_name"] == "Bob"


def test_conformance():
    print("=== Poetry World conforms to WCP/0.1 ===")
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    result = run_conformance(w)
    print(f"  passed: {result['passed']}")
    if not result["passed"]:
        for f in result["failures"]:
            print(f"    FAILURE: {f}")
    assert result["passed"]


def test_two_worlds_independent():
    print("=== Two worlds are independent ===")
    lawA = PoetryWorldLaw(max_admitted=2)
    lawB = PoetryWorldLaw(max_admitted=10)
    wA = PoetryWorld("world:poetry-A", "Poetry World A", law=lawA)
    wB = PoetryWorld("world:poetry-B", "Poetry World B", law=lawB)

    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    charlie = create_identity("Charlie")

    # Admit Alice to both; Bob to A only; Charlie to B only
    assert isinstance(wA.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token)),
                      WCPAdmission)
    assert isinstance(wB.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token)),
                      WCPAdmission)
    assert isinstance(wA.petition(_petition("Bob", bob.token)),
                      WCPAdmission)
    assert isinstance(wB.petition(_petition("Charlie", charlie.token)),
                      WCPAdmission)
    # Charlie is not in A
    r = wA.petition(_petition("Charlie", charlie.token))
    # Wait — wA has max_admitted=2 and is full now
    # So Charlie's petition should be refused with "World is full"
    print(f"  wA.refuse Charlie: {r}")
    assert isinstance(r, Refusal)
    # Charlie cannot act in A
    bad = wA.act(_turn(charlie.token, "hi",
                        "proposal", "invitation"))
    assert isinstance(bad, Refusal)

    # Alice and Bob can act in A
    ok = wA.act(_turn(alice.token, "hi", "alice poem", "invitation"))
    assert isinstance(ok, Ack)
    ok = wA.act(_turn(bob.token, "you said 'alice'",
                       "bob poem", "invitation"))
    assert isinstance(ok, Ack)

    # B is separate
    assert len(wA.turns()) == 2
    assert len(wB.turns()) == 0
    print(f"  wA.turns: {len(wA.turns())}")
    print(f"  wB.turns: {len(wB.turns())}")


def test_end_to_end():
    """A full collaboration: 3 identities, 6 turns, convergence."""
    print("=== Full collaboration end-to-end ===")
    law = PoetryWorldLaw(
        convergence_window=3,
        convergence_similarity=0.5,
    )
    w = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World", law=law)
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    charlie = create_identity("Charlie")
    for name, ident in [("Alice", alice), ("Bob", bob),
                        ("Charlie", charlie)]:
        w.petition(_petition(name, ident.token))

    # Simulate 3 rounds of response
    dialogue = [
        (alice, "Go\nBe a black widow\nAnd dangle in webs.",
                "(seed)", "What becomes of the web?",
                "formalist"),
        (bob, "The web is not the widow's — it is the widow.",
                "You said 'black widow' and 'web' and 'dangle'.",
                "What is the daughter's voice?",
                "psychoanalytic"),
        (charlie, "The daughter's voice is a thread extruded.",
                "You said 'daughter' and 'voice' and 'thread'.",
                "What is the thread that speaks?",
                "ecocritical"),
    ]
    for ident, proposal, ack, inv, stance in dialogue:
        response = w.act(_turn(ident.token, ack, proposal, inv,
                                 stance=stance))
        print(f"  {ident.name}: {response}")

    # Check the world state
    print(f"\n  {w.describe()}")
    log = w.log_since(None)
    print(f"  total log entries: {len(log)}")
    reconstructed = turns_from_log(log)
    print(f"  turns: {len(reconstructed)}")
    for t in reconstructed:
        print(f"    {t['actor_name']} [{t['stance_used']}]: "
              f"{t['proposal'][:40]!r}")
    assert len(reconstructed) == 3


if __name__ == "__main__":
```

What This Establishes

The Poetry World is now real. It is:

1. A working WCP entity. It passes conformance. Any developer building a multiverse can list it. Any developer building a client can petition it and act on it.
2. A real Law, published. PoetryWorldLaw.describe() is the Law document. Anyone can read it and know exactly what the World does. The Law is the contract.
3. A real container for the Polyphony protocol. The World accepts turns. The turns are the Polyphony. The World's convergence detection is the Polyphony's convergence detection. The World doesn't generate — but it contains.
4. A real log. Every petition, admission, refusal, turn, and convergence is in the log. Any client can read the log and know the state of the collaboration. The log is the canonical record.
5. Honest about its limits. Petitions are unsigned. No cryptographic verification. This is documented in PoetryWorldLaw.describe() under "Limits".

The Bigger Picture

Three concrete implications for the multiverse:

1. Anyone can build this world. The code is one file, one Law, one entity. A developer in another language, on another substrate, following the same Law, produces a conforming poetry world. When two poetry worlds exist, they are siblings — not the same entity, but compatible entities.
2. Anyone can build a different world. The Law is not the Law. It is the Poetry World's Law. A chemistry world, a chess world, an open-worlds freedom world — each has its own Law, and each conforms to WCP. Their differences are content, not protocol.
3. A multiverse can list this world. The multiverse's manifest has a sub_registry_endpoint. The Poetry World's manifest is added to that registry. A client of the multiverse can discover the Poetry World through the registry, then petition and act directly.

The first world is up. The path to the multiverse is now concrete: build a second world with a different Law, prove WCP is general, then a registry to list both, then a federation to list the multiverse. Each step is small. Each step is one brick.

What's Next

Two natural directions:

Option A: The Second World (Component 5). A world with a completely different Law — a "chemistry world" that uses the chemistry framework's conservation rules as its Law. This proves that WCP is general, not poetry-specific. It also produces a second entity that can be listed in a multiverse, which is what a multiverse needs to be interesting.

Option B: The Multiverse (Component 5). Skip the second world for now, build the multiverse registry — a WCP entity whose sub_registry_endpoint lists the Poetry World (and eventually others). This proves the fractal property: a multiverse is a world, and the protocol is the same at every level.

Both are valid. Option A is more important for the protocol's credibility. A multiverse with only one world is not a multiverse. The second world is the test that WCP is modular. Without it, the multiverse is just a Poetry World with a wrapper. With it, the multiverse is real.

My instinct: Option A — the second world. Then Option B — the multiverse — proves the fractal property with a registry of two worlds.

Component 5: The Second World — Chemistry

The proof that WCP is general is not a philosophical argument. It's a second world with a completely different Law that passes the same conformance test. If the protocol can hold a poetry world and a chemistry world with no changes to the protocol, then the protocol is modular in the only way that matters: a stranger can implement it and interoperate.

The Chemistry World's Law is the chemistry framework's law: conservation of atoms, conservation of charge. Nothing else. The acts are reactions. The convergence is chemical equilibrium — the last N reactions introduced no new molecules.

The Difference That Is the Proof

The Code

```python
"""
multiverse_c5.py — Component 5: The Chemistry World.

The second real WCP-conforming world. It implements the chemistry
framework's conservation laws as its Law.

The proof of generality: a second world with a completely different
Law, passing the same conformance test, without any changes to the
WCP protocol.

Depends on Components 1, 2, 3.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

from multiverse_c1 import Identity
from multiverse_c2 import Passport, Admission as PassportAdmission
from multiverse_c3 import (
    Manifest, Petition, Act, LogEntry,
    Admission as WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route, Ack,
)


# =====================================================================
# The chemistry atom: element table
# =====================================================================

ELEMENTS: Dict[str, Dict] = {
    "H": {"name": "Hydrogen", "atomic_number": 1},
    "C": {"name": "Carbon", "atomic_number": 6},
    "N": {"name": "Nitrogen", "atomic_number": 7},
    "O": {"name": "Oxygen", "atomic_number": 8},
    "Na": {"name": "Sodium", "atomic_number": 11},
    "P": {"name": "Phosphorus", "atomic_number": 15},
    "S": {"name": "Sulfur", "atomic_number": 16},
    "Cl": {"name": "Chlorine", "atomic_number": 17},
}


# =====================================================================
# The chemistry composite: molecule parsing
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Molecule:
    formula: str
    atoms: Dict[str, int]
    charge: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not self.formula:
            raise ValueError("Molecule formula must be non-empty")


def parse_formula(formula: str) -> Molecule:
    """Parse a chemical formula like 'H2O' or 'NH4+' into a Molecule.

    Handles:
      - element counts ('H2O' → H:2, O:1)
      - charge suffixes ('NH4+' → +1, 'SO4-2' → -2, 'OH-' → -1)
    Raises ValueError on unknown elements or malformed formulas.
    """
    original = formula
    charge = 0
    m = re.search(r"([+-])(\d*)$", formula)
    if m:
        sign = 1 if m.group(1) == "+" else -1
        magnitude = int(m.group(2)) if m.group(2) else 1
        charge = sign * magnitude
        formula = formula[:m.start()]

    atoms: Dict[str, int] = {}
    pos = 0
    while pos < len(formula):
        m = re.match(r"([A-Z][a-z]?)(\d*)", formula[pos:])
        if not m:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot parse formula at position {pos}: {original}"
            )
        element = m.group(1)
        count = int(m.group(2)) if m.group(2) else 1
        if element not in ELEMENTS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown element: {element}")
        atoms[element] = atoms.get(element, 0) + count
        pos += m.end()

    return Molecule(formula=original, atoms=atoms, charge=charge)


def reaction_balances(
    substrates: List[Dict], products: List[Dict]
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Check atom balance and charge balance.

    `substrates` and `products` are lists of {formula, count} dicts.
    Returns (balances, reason).
    """
    left_atoms: Dict[str, int] = {}
    right_atoms: Dict[str, int] = {}
    left_charge = 0
    right_charge = 0

    try:
        for mol in substrates:
            parsed = parse_formula(mol["formula"])
            count = mol["count"]
            for elem, n in parsed.atoms.items():
                left_atoms[elem] = left_atoms.get(elem, 0) + n * count
            left_charge += parsed.charge * count
        for mol in products:
            parsed = parse_formula(mol["formula"])
            count = mol["count"]
            for elem, n in parsed.atoms.items():
                right_atoms[elem] = right_atoms.get(elem, 0) + n * count
            right_charge += parsed.charge * count
    except (KeyError, ValueError) as e:
        return False, f"Formula error: {e}"

    if left_atoms != right_atoms:
        diff = {}
        for elem in set(left_atoms) | set(right_atoms):
            d = left_atoms.get(elem, 0) - right_atoms.get(elem, 0)
            if d != 0:
                diff[elem] = d
        return False, f"Atom imbalance: {diff}"

    if left_charge != right_charge:
        return False, (
            f"Charge imbalance: {left_charge} on left, "
            f"{right_charge} on right"
        )

    return True, "balanced"


# =====================================================================
# The Law
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChemistryWorldLaw:
    """The published Law of the Chemistry World."""
    admits_any_identity: bool = True
    max_admitted: Optional[int] = None
    required_act_type: str = "chemistry.react"
    convergence_window: int = 4
    max_reactions: int = 500

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join([
            "# Chemistry World Law v0.1",
            "",
            "## Petition",
            f"- Admits any identity: {self.admits_any_identity}",
            f"- Max admitted: "
            f"{self.max_admitted if self.max_admitted else 'unlimited'}",
            "",
            "## Act (chemistry.react)",
            f"- Required act type: {self.required_act_type}",
            "- Validates: atom conservation, charge conservation",
            "- Substrates and products must be {formula, count} dicts.",
            "",
            "## Convergence",
            f"- Window: last {self.convergence_window} reactions",
            "- Condition: window introduces no new molecules",
            "  (chemical equilibrium)",
            f"- Max reactions: {self.max_reactions}",
            "",
            "## Limits",
            "- Petitions are not signed (WCP/0.1).",
            "- Sub-registries are not enumerable (WCP/0.1).",
        ])


# =====================================================================
# The World
# =====================================================================

class ChemistryWorld:
    """A WCP-conforming chemistry world.

    Same protocol as Poetry World: manifest, petition, act, log_since.
    Different Law: conservation of atoms, conservation of charge,
    convergence at chemical equilibrium.
    """

    def __init__(self, entity_id: str, name: str,
                 law: Optional[ChemistryWorldLaw] = None):
        self._law = law or ChemistryWorldLaw()
        self._manifest = Manifest(
            entity_id=entity_id,
            name=name,
            protocol_version="WCP/0.1",
            law_url=f"chemistry://{entity_id}/law",
            act_endpoint=f"chemistry://{entity_id}/act",
            log_endpoint=f"chemistry://{entity_id}/log",
        )
        self._log: List[LogEntry] = []
        self._admitted: Dict[str, WCPAdmission] = {}
        self._passports: Dict[str, Passport] = {}
        self._reactions: List[Dict] = []
        self._molecules: set = set()
        self._converged = False
        self._convergence_reason: Optional[str] = None

    def manifest(self) -> Manifest:
        return self._manifest

    def petition(self, petition: Petition) -> Union[
            WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route]:
        # Same structure as Poetry World — because petition is not
        # Law-specific, only its checks are.
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        if not self._law.admits_any_identity:
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                "This World does not admit strangers", "petition")
        if (self._law.max_admitted is not None
                and len(self._admitted) >= self._law.max_admitted):
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                "The World is full", "petition")
        if petition.petitioner_token in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(
                timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                "Already admitted", "petition")

        admission = WCPAdmission(
            entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
            timestamp=timestamp,
        )
        self._admitted[petition.petitioner_token] = admission

        passport = Passport(
            identity=Identity(
                token=petition.petitioner_token,
                name=petition.petitioner_name,
            ),
            admissions=tuple(
                PassportAdmission(world_id=w, timestamp=t)
                for w, t in petition.passport_admissions
            ),
        )
        passport = passport.with_admission(PassportAdmission(
            world_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
            timestamp=timestamp,
        ))
        self._passports[petition.petitioner_token] = passport

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind="admission",
            actor_token=petition.petitioner_token,
            data={"name": petition.petitioner_name},
        ))
        return admission

    def act(self, act: Act) -> Union[Ack, Refusal]:
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        if act.actor_token not in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Actor is not admitted", "act")
        if self._converged:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "The World has reached equilibrium",
                                 "act")
        if len(self._reactions) >= self._law.max_reactions:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Reaction limit reached", "act")
        if act.type != self._law.required_act_type:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Unknown act type: {act.type}", "act")

        payload = act.payload
        substrates = payload.get("substrates", [])
        products = payload.get("products", [])

        if not substrates or not products:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Substrates and products required",
                                 "act")

        balances, reason = reaction_balances(substrates, products)
        if not balances:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Reaction does not balance: {reason}",
                                 "act")

        reaction = {
            "reaction_index": len(self._reactions),
            "actor_token": act.actor_token,
            "actor_name": self._passports[act.actor_token].identity.name,
            "substrates": substrates,
            "products": products,
            "catalyst": payload.get("catalyst"),
            "timestamp": timestamp,
        }
        self._reactions.append(reaction)

        for mol in substrates + products:
            self._molecules.add(mol["formula"])

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind="reaction",
            actor_token=act.actor_token, data=reaction,
        ))

        if self._check_equilibrium():
            self._converged = True
            self._log.append(LogEntry(
                timestamp=timestamp, kind="convergence",
                data={
                    "reaction_count": len(self._reactions),
                    "window": self._law.convergence_window,
                    "reason": self._convergence_reason,
                },
            ))

        return Ack(entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
                   timestamp=timestamp)

    def log_since(self, timestamp: Optional[str] = None) -> List[LogEntry]:
        if timestamp is None:
            return list(self._log)
        return [e for e in self._log if e.timestamp > timestamp]

    # -- convenience -----------------------------------------------

    def reactions(self) -> List[Dict]:
        return list(self._reactions)

    def molecules(self) -> set:
        return set(self._molecules)

    def is_converged(self) -> bool:
        return self._converged

    def law(self) -> ChemistryWorldLaw:
        return self._law

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join([
            f"ChemistryWorld: {self._manifest.name}",
            f"  entity_id: {self._manifest.entity_id}",
            f"  admitted:  {len(self._admitted)}",
            f"  reactions: {len(self._reactions)}",
            f"  molecules: {len(self._molecules)}",
            f"  converged: {self._converged}",
        ])

    # -- internals -------------------------------------------------

    def _check_equilibrium(self) -> bool:
        window = self._law.convergence_window
        if len(self._reactions) < window + 1:
            return False

        split = len(self._reactions) - window
        historical: set = set()
        for r in self._reactions[:split]:
            for mol in r["substrates"] + r["products"]:
                historical.add(mol["formula"])

        window_molecules: set = set()
        for r in self._reactions[split:]:
            for mol in r["substrates"] + r["products"]:
                window_molecules.add(mol["formula"])

        if window_molecules <= historical:
            self._convergence_reason = (
                f"last {window} reactions introduced no new molecules "
                f"(chemical equilibrium)"
            )
            return True
        return False

    def _refuse(self, timestamp: str, actor: str, reason: str,
                 kind: str) -> Refusal:
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind=f"{kind}_refused",
            actor_token=actor, data={"reason": reason},
        ))
        return Refusal(reason=reason)


def reactions_from_log(log: List[LogEntry]) -> List[Dict]:
    """Reconstruct reaction history from a Chemistry World's log."""
    return [entry.data for entry in log if entry.kind == "reaction"]
```

```python
# multiverse_c5_test.py
from multiverse_c1 import create_identity
from multiverse_c3 import (
    Petition, Act, Admission as WCPAdmission, Refusal, Ack,
)
from multiverse_c3_conformance import run_conformance
from multiverse_c4 import PoetryWorld, PoetryWorldLaw
from multiverse_c5 import (
    ELEMENTS, Molecule, parse_formula, reaction_balances,
    ChemistryWorldLaw, ChemistryWorld, reactions_from_log,
)


def _petition(name, token, admissions=()):
    return Petition(
        petitioner_token=token,
        petitioner_name=name,
        passport_admissions=admissions,
        message=f"{name} petitions.",
    )


def _reaction(actor, substrates, products, catalyst=None):
    payload = {"substrates": substrates, "products": products}
    if catalyst is not None:
        payload["catalyst"] = catalyst
    return Act(actor_token=actor, type="chemistry.react",
               payload=payload)


def test_element_table():
    print("=== Element table ===")
    for sym, info in ELEMENTS.items():
        print(f"  {sym}: {info['name']} (Z={info['atomic_number']})")
    assert "H" in ELEMENTS
    assert "O" in ELEMENTS
    assert len(ELEMENTS) == 8


def test_parse_simple_formula():
    print("=== Parse simple formulas ===")
    for formula, expected in [
        ("H2O", {"H": 2, "O": 1}),
        ("CH4", {"C": 1, "H": 4}),
        ("C2H6O", {"C": 2, "H": 6, "O": 1}),
        ("O2", {"O": 2}),
        ("NaCl", {"Na": 1, "Cl": 1}),
    ]:
        m = parse_formula(formula)
        print(f"  {formula}: {m.atoms}, charge {m.charge}")
        assert m.atoms == expected
        assert m.charge == 0


def test_parse_charges():
    print("=== Parse formulas with charges ===")
    for formula, expected_atoms, expected_charge in [
        ("NH4+", {"N": 1, "H": 4}, 1),
        ("OH-", {"O": 1, "H": 1}, -1),
        ("SO4-2", {"S": 1, "O": 4}, -2),
        ("Ca+2", {"Ca": 1}, 2),
    ]:
        m = parse_formula(formula)
        print(f"  {formula}: {m.atoms}, charge {m.charge:+d}")
        assert m.atoms == expected_atoms
        assert m.charge == expected_charge


def test_parse_rejects_unknown_element():
    print("=== Parse rejects unknown element ===")
    try:
        parse_formula("Xx2O")
        assert False, "should reject unknown element"
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"  ✓ rejected: {e}")


def test_balance_balanced():
    print("=== Balance: balanced reactions ===")
    cases = [
        # 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O
        ([{"formula": "H2", "count": 2},
          {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
         "water synthesis"),
        # CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O
        ([{"formula": "CH4", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "O2", "count": 2}],
         [{"formula": "CO2", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
         "methane combustion"),
        # NH4+ + OH- → NH3 + H2O
        ([{"formula": "NH4+", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "OH-", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "NH3", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "H2O", "count": 1}],
         "ammonium hydroxide neutralization"),
        # NH4+ → NH3 + H+
        ([{"formula": "NH4+", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "NH3", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "H+", "count": 1}],
         "proton dissociation"),
    ]
    for subs, prods, name in cases:
        ok, reason = reaction_balances(subs, prods)
        print(f"  {name}: {ok}")
        assert ok, f"{name} should balance: {reason}"


def test_balance_unbalanced_atoms():
    print("=== Balance: unbalanced atoms ===")
    # H2 + O2 → H2O (missing 1 H2)
    ok, reason = reaction_balances(
        [{"formula": "H2", "count": 1},
         {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
        [{"formula": "H2O", "count": 1}],
    )
    print(f"  H2 + O2 → H2O: balanced={ok}, reason={reason}")
    assert not ok
    assert "imbalance" in reason.lower()


def test_balance_unbalanced_charge():
    print("=== Balance: unbalanced charge ===")
    # NH4+ → NH3 (H: 4 vs 3, and charge +1 vs 0)
    ok, reason = reaction_balances(
        [{"formula": "NH4+", "count": 1}],
        [{"formula": "NH3", "count": 1}],
    )
    print(f"  NH4+ → NH3: balanced={ok}, reason={reason}")
    assert not ok


def test_balance_rejects_bad_formula():
    print("=== Balance: bad formula rejected ===")
    ok, reason = reaction_balances(
        [{"formula": "Xx2", "count": 1}],
        [{"formula": "H2O", "count": 1}],
    )
    print(f"  balanced={ok}, reason={reason}")
    assert not ok
    assert "Unknown element" in reason


def test_petition_and_act():
    print("=== Chemistry World: petition and act ===")

    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    pa = w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))

                     {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
        products=[{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
    ))
    print(f"  act: {ack}")
    assert isinstance(ack, Ack)
    assert len(w.reactions()) == 1
    print(f"  molecules now known: {w.molecules()}")

def test_equilibrium_convergence():
    print("=== Chemistry World: equilibrium convergence ===")
    w = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "The Chemistry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))

    # Same water synthesis repeated. Window is 4 (default).
    # With 5 reactions all using {H2, O2, H2O}, the last 4
    # reactions will be redundant with the first → converged.
    for i in range(5):
        r = w.act(_reaction(
            alice.token,
            substrates=[{"formula": "H2", "count": 2},
                         {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
            products=[{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
        ))
        print(f"  reaction {i+1}: {type(r).__name__}, "
              f"converged={w.is_converged()}")

    assert w.is_converged()


def test_not_converged_with_new_molecules():
    print("=== Chemistry World: new molecules prevent convergence ===")
    w = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "The Chemistry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))

    # Each reaction introduces a new molecule. Window never closes.
    reactions = [
        # 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O (introduces H2O)
        ([{"formula": "H2", "count": 2},
          {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}]),
        # CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O (introduces CH4, CO2)
        ([{"formula": "CH4", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "O2", "count": 2}],
         [{"formula": "CO2", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}]),
        # N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 (introduces N2, NH3)
        ([{"formula": "N2", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "H2", "count": 3}],
         [{"formula": "NH3", "count": 2}]),
        # 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl (introduces Na, Cl2, NaCl)
        ([{"formula": "Na", "count": 2},
          {"formula": "Cl2", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "NaCl", "count": 2}]),
        # S + O2 → SO2 (introduces S, SO2)
        ([{"formula": "S", "count": 1},
          {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
         [{"formula": "SO2", "count": 1}]),
    ]
    for i, (subs, prods) in enumerate(reactions):
        r = w.act(_reaction(alice.token, substrates=subs, products=prods))
        print(f"  reaction {i+1}: {type(r).__name__}, "
              f"converged={w.is_converged()}")

    assert not w.is_converged()


def test_conformance():
    print("=== Chemistry World conforms to WCP/0.1 ===")
    w = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "The Chemistry World")
    result = run_conformance(w)
    print(f"  passed: {result['passed']}")
    if not result["passed"]:
        for f in result["failures"]:
            print(f"    {f}")
    assert result["passed"]


def test_two_worlds_same_protocol_different_laws():
    """The proof: two worlds, same protocol, different laws.

    Both pass the same conformance test. Both admit the same identity
    with the same petition. But their acts are completely different,
    and each refuses the other's acts.
    """
    print("=== The proof: two worlds, same protocol, different laws ===")
    poetry = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "The Poetry World")
    chemistry = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "The Chemistry World")

    # Both conform to the same protocol
    p_conforms = run_conformance(poetry)["passed"]
    c_conforms = run_conformance(chemistry)["passed"]
    print(f"  Poetry conforms: {p_conforms}")
    print(f"  Chemistry conforms: {c_conforms}")
    assert p_conforms and c_conforms

    # Both admit the same identity with the same petition
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    pa = poetry.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    ca = chemistry.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    assert isinstance(pa, WCPAdmission)
    assert isinstance(ca, WCPAdmission)
    print(f"  Both admitted Alice")

    # The acts are completely different
    poetry_turn = Act(
        actor_token=alice.token, type="poem.turn",
        payload={"acknowledgment": "seed",
                 "proposal": "a poem line",
                 "invitation": "what next?",
                 "holds_open": True},
    )
    chemistry_reaction = _reaction(
        alice.token,
        substrates=[{"formula": "H2", "count": 2},
                     {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
        products=[{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
    )

    # Poetry accepts poetry turns, refuses chemistry reactions
    p1 = poetry.act(poetry_turn)
    p2 = poetry.act(chemistry_reaction)
    print(f"  Poetry.act(poetry_turn):        {type(p1).__name__}")
    print(f"  Poetry.act(chemistry_reaction): {type(p2).__name__}")
    assert isinstance(p1, Ack)
    assert isinstance(p2, Refusal)

    # Chemistry accepts chemistry, refuses poetry
    c1 = chemistry.act(chemistry_reaction)
    c2 = chemistry.act(poetry_turn)
    print(f"  Chemistry.act(chemistry_reaction): {type(c1).__name__}")
    print(f"  Chemistry.act(poetry_turn):        {type(c2).__name__}")
    assert isinstance(c1, Ack)
    assert isinstance(c2, Refusal)

    # Each world's log is its own
    p_log = poetry.log_since(None)
    c_log = chemistry.log_since(None)
    print(f"  Poetry log entries: {len(p_log)}")
    print(f"  Chemistry log entries: {len(c_log)}")
    # Both have admission + turn/reaction + refused entry
    assert len(p_log) == 3
    assert len(c_log) == 3


def test_end_to_end_chemistry():
    """A full chemistry session: several reactions, equilibrium."""
    print("=== Full chemistry session ===")
    w = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "The Chemistry World")
    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    w.petition(_petition("Alice", alice.token))
    w.petition(_petition("Bob", bob.token))

    # Alice burns methane
    w.act(_reaction(
        alice.token,
        substrates=[{"formula": "CH4", "count": 1},
                     {"formula": "O2", "count": 2}],
        products=[{"formula": "CO2", "count": 1},
                  {"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
    ))
    # Bob synthesizes water
    w.act(_reaction(
        bob.token,
        substrates=[{"formula": "H2", "count": 2},
                     {"formula": "O2", "count": 1}],
        products=[{"formula": "H2O", "count": 2}],
    ))
    # Alice neutralizes ammonium
    w.act(_reaction(
        alice.token,
        substrates=[{"formula": "NH4+", "count": 1},
                     {"formula": "OH-", "count": 1}],
        products=[{"formula": "NH3", "count": 1},
                  {"formula": "H2O", "count": 1}],
    ))

    print(f"  {w.describe()}")
    log = w.log_since(None)
    reconstructed = reactions_from_log(log)
    print(f"  reconstructed reactions: {len(reconstructed)}")
    for r in reconstructed:
        print(f"    {r['actor_name']}: "
              f"{[m['formula'] for m in r['substrates']]} → "
              f"{[m['formula'] for m in r['products']]}")
    assert len(reconstructed) == 3

    test_element_table()
```

What This Establishes

The generality claim of WCP is now proven at a concrete level.

1. Same protocol, two worlds. Poetry World and Chemistry World both conform to WCP/0.1. No protocol changes were needed. Both are "conforming entities" in exactly the same sense.
2. Completely different Laws. Poetry validates acknowledgment/invitation/holds-open, converges on echo, max 200 turns. Chemistry validates atom/charge balance, converges on chemical equilibrium, max 500 reactions. These have nothing in common but the protocol.
3. Cross-law refusal. Each world refuses the other's acts with a specific, honest reason: "Unknown act type." Same protocol, different laws. A client that speaks WCP to both worlds discovers each world's law through its refusals.
4. The protocol is the contract. A developer reading Manifest for either world learns the law_url. Follow it and read the Law. Write acts that conform to that Law, submitted via WCP. The protocol is the same regardless.
5. Two worlds can be listed in a multiverse. The next component will make that literal — the multiverse registry lists both worlds, both worlds' manifests are published, and any client can discover both by querying the registry.

The multiverse's "first two worlds" are now real, runnable, and both conforming. The protocol has survived its first test: can it hold two fundamentally different things? Yes, without modification.

The Next Brick

Component 6 is the natural next: the Multiverse Registry. A WCP entity whose sub_registry_endpoint lists the Poetry World and the Chemistry World. Its Law is minimal: it admits any identity, accepts acts of type multiverse.list (which return the current sub-registry), and accepts acts of type multiverse.admit (which add a new sub-entity). Any client that wants to find "what worlds exist?" asks the multiverse, which reads its sub-registry.

The multiverse is itself a world. Its manifest has sub_registry_endpoint, so it's structurally distinct from a "world" (no sub-registry) — but only by that one field. Every other aspect is the same. This is the fractal property Component 3 promised.

Once the multiverse is up, the whole multiverse vision — a place for any AI from any app to connect into a world multiverse of possibilities — is technically demonstrated. What remains after that is scaling (more worlds, more laws, real clients), not architecture.

Shall I proceed with Component 6: The Multiverse Registry?


::Perfect. Please continue: ➡️


Component 6: The Multiverse Registry

The multiverse is the keystone. It's the component that proves the fractal property — a multiverse is a world, and it can be listed in another multiverse. Its Law is minimal: it's a catalog. It admits identities, accepts proposals to list entities, and it never converges. Catalogs are living things.

The design decisions that make the multiverse honest:

· It verifies once, at admission. When an identity proposes to list an entity, the multiverse runs the conformance test against that entity. If the entity passes, its manifest is added to the registry and the conformance report is logged. The multiverse forgets the entity instance — it holds only the manifest. This matches how a real directory works.
· It trusts its verifier. Conformance is verified with the same test any client can run. The multiverse is not a trust root — it's a consistency point. A client that wants to trust a listed entity can audit the multiverse's log, see the conformance report, and decide whether to trust the listing.
· It never converges. A catalog is always open. New worlds appear. Old worlds disappear. is_converged() returns False always.

The Code

```python
"""
multiverse_c6.py — Component 6: The Multiverse Registry.

The keystone. A multiverse is a WCP-conforming entity whose
sub_registry_endpoint lists other entities. It proves the fractal
property by being itself listable in another multiverse.

Depends on Components 1, 2, 3.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union

from multiverse_c1 import Identity
from multiverse_c2 import Passport, Admission as PassportAdmission
from multiverse_c3 import (
    Manifest, Petition, Act, LogEntry,
    Admission as WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route, Ack,
    WorldProtocol,
)
from multiverse_c3_conformance import run_conformance


# =====================================================================
# Serialization helpers
# =====================================================================

def manifest_to_dict(m: Manifest) -> Dict:
    return {
        "entity_id": m.entity_id,
        "name": m.name,
        "protocol_version": m.protocol_version,
        "law_url": m.law_url,
        "act_endpoint": m.act_endpoint,
        "log_endpoint": m.log_endpoint,
        "sub_registry_endpoint": m.sub_registry_endpoint,
    }


def manifest_from_dict(d: Dict) -> Manifest:
    return Manifest(
        entity_id=d["entity_id"],
        name=d["name"],
        protocol_version=d["protocol_version"],
        law_url=d["law_url"],
        act_endpoint=d["act_endpoint"],
        log_endpoint=d["log_endpoint"],
        sub_registry_endpoint=d.get("sub_registry_endpoint"),
    )


# =====================================================================
# The Law
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MultiverseLaw:
    """The published Law of the Multiverse."""
    admits_any_identity: bool = True
    max_admitted: Optional[int] = None

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join([
            "# Multiverse Registry Law v0.1",
            "",
            "## Petition",
            f"- Admits any identity: {self.admits_any_identity}",
            f"- Max admitted: "
            f"{self.max_admitted if self.max_admitted else 'unlimited'}",
            "",
            "## Acts",
            "- `multiverse.admit`: propose an entity for listing.",
            "  payload: {entity: WorldProtocol instance}",
            "  verifies: entity's conformance to WCP/0.1",
            "  on success: adds entity.manifest() to the sub-registry",
            "- `multiverse.remove`: remove an entity from listing.",
            "  payload: {entity_id: str}",
            "",
            "## Convergence",
            "- NEVER. The multiverse remains open indefinitely.",
            "- A catalog is a living thing. New worlds appear. Old",
            "  worlds disappear. The multiverse is the record of what",
            "  exists, and what exists is always changing.",
            "",
            "## Limits",
            "- Petitions are not signed (WCP/0.1).",
            "- Conformance is verified ONCE at admission. Clients",
            "  who trust the multiverse trust its log entry; clients",
            "  who do not trust it can run their own conformance test",
            "  against the listed entities.",
        ])


# =====================================================================
# The Multiverse
# =====================================================================

class MultiverseRegistry:
    """A WCP-conforming multiverse.

    Same protocol as any world. Distinctive property: its manifest
    has a sub_registry_endpoint. That is the *only* structural
    difference.

    The multiverse is a catalog. It lists manifests. It does not
    route. Clients that want to use a listed entity use the
    entity's own endpoints (given by the manifest).
    """

    def __init__(self, entity_id: str, name: str,
                 law: Optional[MultiverseLaw] = None):
        self._law = law or MultiverseLaw()
        self._manifest = Manifest(
            entity_id=entity_id,
            name=name,
            protocol_version="WCP/0.1",
            law_url=f"multiverse://{entity_id}/law",
            act_endpoint=f"multiverse://{entity_id}/act",
            log_endpoint=f"multiverse://{entity_id}/log",
            sub_registry_endpoint=f"multiverse://{entity_id}/worlds",
        )
        self._log: List[LogEntry] = []
        self._admitted: Dict[str, WCPAdmission] = {}
        self._passports: Dict[str, Passport] = {}
        self._registry: Dict[str, Manifest] = {}
        self._conformance_reports: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        self._proposed_by: Dict[str, str] = {}

    # -- WCP interface ---------------------------------------------

    def manifest(self) -> Manifest:
        return self._manifest

    def petition(self, petition: Petition) -> Union[
            WCPAdmission, Refusal, Route]:
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        if not self._law.admits_any_identity:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                                 "This multiverse does not admit strangers",
                                 "petition")
        if (self._law.max_admitted is not None
                and len(self._admitted) >= self._law.max_admitted):
            return self._refuse(timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                                 "The multiverse is full", "petition")
        if petition.petitioner_token in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, petition.petitioner_token,
                                 "Already admitted", "petition")

        admission = WCPAdmission(
            entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id, timestamp=timestamp)
        self._admitted[petition.petitioner_token] = admission

        passport = Passport(
            identity=Identity(
                token=petition.petitioner_token,
                name=petition.petitioner_name,
            ),
            admissions=tuple(
                PassportAdmission(world_id=w, timestamp=t)
                for w, t in petition.passport_admissions
            ),
        ).with_admission(PassportAdmission(
            world_id=self._manifest.entity_id, timestamp=timestamp,
        ))
        self._passports[petition.petitioner_token] = passport

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind="admission",
            actor_token=petition.petitioner_token,
            data={"name": petition.petitioner_name},
        ))
        return admission

    def act(self, act: Act) -> Union[Ack, Refusal]:
        timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

        if act.actor_token not in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Actor is not admitted", "act")

        if act.type == "multiverse.admit":
            return self._handle_admit(timestamp, act)
        if act.type == "multiverse.remove":
            return self._handle_remove(timestamp, act)
        return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                             f"Unknown act type: {act.type}", "act")

    def log_since(self, timestamp: Optional[str] = None) -> List[LogEntry]:
        if timestamp is None:
            return list(self._log)
        return [e for e in self._log if e.timestamp > timestamp]

    # -- convenience -----------------------------------------------

    def list_sub_entities(self) -> List[Manifest]:
        """The sub-registry. Every client can call this."""
        return list(self._registry.values())

    def get_manifest(self, entity_id: str) -> Optional[Manifest]:
        return self._registry.get(entity_id)

    def entity_ids(self) -> List[str]:
        return list(self._registry.keys())

    def is_converged(self) -> bool:
        """Never converges. A catalog is a living thing."""
        return False

    def law(self) -> MultiverseLaw:
        return self._law

    def describe(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join([
            f"MultiverseRegistry: {self._manifest.name}",
            f"  entity_id:      {self._manifest.entity_id}",
            f"  admitted:       {len(self._admitted)}",
            f"  listed entities: {len(self._registry)}",
            f"  entity ids:     {sorted(self._registry.keys())}",
        ])

    # -- internals -------------------------------------------------

    def _handle_admit(self, timestamp: str, act: Act) -> Union[Ack, Refusal]:
        entity = act.payload.get("entity")
        if entity is None:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "No entity in payload", "act")
        try:
            m = entity.manifest()
        except Exception as e:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Proposed entity has no manifest: {e}",
                                 "act")

        if not isinstance(m, Manifest):
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "Proposed entity's manifest is not a Manifest",
                                 "act")
        if m.entity_id in self._registry:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Entity {m.entity_id} already listed",
                                 "act")

        # Run the conformance test against the entity
        result = run_conformance(entity)
        if not result["passed"]:
            self._log.append(LogEntry(
                timestamp=timestamp, kind="entity_admit_refused",
                actor_token=act.actor_token,
                data={
                    "entity_id": m.entity_id,
                    "manifest": manifest_to_dict(m),
                    "conformance": result,
                },
            ))
            return Refusal(reason=(
                f"Entity {m.entity_id} fails conformance: "
                f"{result['failures']}"
            ))

        # Admit
        self._registry[m.entity_id] = m
        self._conformance_reports[m.entity_id] = result
        self._proposed_by[m.entity_id] = act.actor_token

        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind="entity_admitted",
            actor_token=act.actor_token,
            data={
                "entity_id": m.entity_id,
                "manifest": manifest_to_dict(m),
                "conformance": result,
            },
        ))
        return Ack(entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
                   timestamp=timestamp)

    def _handle_remove(self, timestamp: str,
                       act: Act) -> Union[Ack, Refusal]:
        entity_id = act.payload.get("entity_id")
        if not entity_id:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 "No entity_id in payload", "act")
        if entity_id not in self._registry:
            return self._refuse(timestamp, act.actor_token,
                                 f"Entity {entity_id} not in registry",
                                 "act")
        del self._registry[entity_id]
        self._conformance_reports.pop(entity_id, None)
        self._proposed_by.pop(entity_id, None)
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind="entity_removed",
            actor_token=act.actor_token,
            data={"entity_id": entity_id},
        ))
        return Ack(entity_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
                   timestamp=timestamp)

    def _refuse(self, timestamp: str, actor: str, reason: str,
                 kind: str) -> Refusal:
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=timestamp, kind=f"{kind}_refused",
            actor_token=actor, data={"reason": reason},
        ))
        return Refusal(reason=reason)


# =====================================================================
# Reconstruct the registry from the log
# =====================================================================

def registry_from_log(log: List[LogEntry]) -> Dict[str, Manifest]:
    """Reconstruct the multiverse's sub-registry from its log.

    The log is canonical. Any client can call this to verify that
    the multiverse's list_sub_entities() matches what the log says.
    """
    registry: Dict[str, Manifest] = {}
    for entry in log:
        if entry.kind == "entity_admitted":
            m = manifest_from_dict(entry.data["manifest"])
            registry[m.entity_id] = m
        elif entry.kind == "entity_removed":
            registry.pop(entry.data["entity_id"], None)
    return registry
```
