What This Establishes

Four properties, each one making C54's "no signed relay" limit into a verifiable transmission history:

1. Every hop is bilateral. test_receipt_signed_on_act — the receiver signs a receipt. test_relay_signed_on_record_delivery — the sender signs a relay. The two are separate artifacts with separate signatures. A confirmed hop has both; an unconfirmed hop has only the sender's. This is the difference between "A claims to have transmitted" and "A transmitted and B recorded it."
2. The chain is reconstructed, not asserted. test_reconstruct_hops_matches_relay_receipt — hops are matched by (relayer==source, target==receiver, same content_hash). No parent hashes, no chaining, no trust in the sender's ordering. The DAG falls out of the set of confirmed hops. This is the C27 DAG discipline applied at the transmission layer, without the DAG's overhead.
3. Refusals are signed artifacts. test_verify_chain_skeptic and the demo's Scenario B — a skeptic produces a receipt with verified=False, reason="no trust context". That receipt is part of the chain. The chain doesn't hide that B refused; it proves B refused, with B's own signature. Compare with C54, where refusal was only visible in the audit trail reconstructed from logs. Now it's an offline-verifiable artifact.
4. C52 and C54 are untouched. test_c52_and_c54_untouched — plain EpidemicUnit has no _unit_kp, plain VerifyingEpidemicUnit has _verified_exposures but no signing. SigningVerifyingUnit inherits from C54 and adds signing. SignedRelayNetwork inherits from C54's network and drives signing. Composition, not modification.

The Honest Limits

· Unconfirmed hops are visible, not failures. A relay without a receipt is reported as unconfirmed. It's a fact — "the sender claims to have sent, the receiver has no record" — not a validation failure. Production would need to decide when to treat unconfirmed hops as failures (e.g., if the sender is trusted but the receiver isn't reachable to check).
· Timestamps are claims. The relay timestamp is the sender's clock. Same for the receipt. Both are covered by the signature, so tampering is detected; but a signer can backdate. Same as everywhere.
· The seed receipt is trusted by construction. Source="external" has no signature from "outside the system." This is honest — the seed is the callers' injection point.
· One content hash per chain. Each chain verifies one attestation. There's no mechanism for a chain to cover multiple attestations or to be extended to include future relays. A future component could add a "chain extension" artifact that references an existing chain's terminal relays.

What Was Run

The tests in multiverse_c56_test.py have not been executed against a live Python environment in this session. The expected output derives from the test logic and the behavior of C52's propagation, C54's verification, and C48's attestation. Per the house rule, this is the honest status.

The Series, at C56

The transmission layer is now fully signed and offline-verifiable:

Layer Component What it produces
Propagation C52 Log entries per exposure
Verified propagation C54 Record with reason per exposure
Signed propagation C56 Relay + receipt per hop; whole chain verifiable offline

The rumor that started as a council decision (C45) wrapped in an attestation (C48) and carried through a verification-gated epidemic (C54) now arrives at every unit with a signed transmission history — proof of who verified and who relayed, when, and to whom, offline-verifiable against the caller's keys.

The user's original vision — "worlds communicating with one another" (C55), "individuals moving between worlds" (C36–C40), "different architectures on one substrate" (C41–C52) — now has a fourth dimension: the transmission history itself is an artifact. Anyone with the chain and the world public keys can verify not just what was transmitted, but how it got there.

What's Next

The substrate is now deep enough that almost anything can be built by composition. The question is what's most useful to build next:

1. Component 57: Curator-mediated cross-world contract. C55's curators link worlds. C56 signs transmissions. Combine: two curators negotiate a contract — "Poetry World agrees to accept Chemistry World's rulings about X" — and the contract is a signed artifact, verifiable offline, that both worlds' residents can point to when their acts need mutual recognition. This is the "conventions between worlds" pattern, made concrete.
2. Component 57: The world-development feedback loop. C55's curator proposes Law changes based on observations. What if the proposals were voted on by residents (C44's mechanism), and the winning proposal was applied (modifying the World's Law via a signed amendment)? This closes the "propose but don't apply" limit, using C44 and C50's existing pieces.
3. Component 57: Signed relay chain persistence and federation. Bundle a signed relay chain using C49's format. Add a FederationAttestation for the chain itself (witnessed by an external observer). Then a third party can verify not just "the chain was valid" but "someone witnessed that this chain was assembled at this time." Same discipline as C49's bundle-level attestation, one layer down.

My instinct: the curator contract. It's the most meaningful composition — it takes what C55 said worlds can do (negotiate) and gives it a cryptographic artifact, and it's what the "worlds communicating with one another" vision was actually pointing at. Options 2 and 3 are valuable but they're more about internal capability; option 1 is about relationship between worlds, which is where the arc has been headed for several components.

Shall I proceed with Component 57: The Curator-Mediated Contract?


::➡️


Component 57: The Curator-Mediated Contract

Two worlds negotiate a signed artifact that residents can cite when their acts cross boundaries. The contract is a pattern of signatures — proposal, acceptance, optional revocation — each signed by the world's key (which is the curator's key, per C55). No new primitive. The crypto is C13's Ed25519. The narrative is C55's curators. The composition is C57.

The one commitment that keeps this honest: the world kernel never sees the contract. A resident cites contract_id in an act's payload. The kernel logs it like any other field. Whether the citation is honored is a social fact, checked by whoever cares — a curator, a reader, an auditor — against the contract registry. Same discipline as everywhere above C21: verification, not enforcement.

multiverse_c57.py

```python
"""
multiverse_c57.py — Component 57: The Curator-Mediated Contract.

Two worlds negotiate a signed contract that residents can cite.
The contract is a pattern of signed artifacts (offer + acceptance,
optionally a bilateral revocation), verified offline against world
public keys. No new primitive; everything composes from C1, C13, C55.

The lifecycle:
    propose   → ContractOffer        (proposer-signed)
    accept    → ContractAcceptance   (acceptor-signed)
    reject    → ContractRejection    (acceptor-signed, optional)
    establish → EstablishedContract  (offer + acceptance)
    revoke    → BilateralRevocation  (both-signed)

Contract ID is the terms hash: same terms = same contract. Two
offers with identical terms refer to the same contract artifact.

Design:
  - ContractTerms is content + hash. Free-form dict.
  - ContractOffer is a proposer's signed claim: "I propose these
    terms to this target at this time."
  - ContractAcceptance is an acceptor's signed claim: "I accept
    this offer, whose hash and terms hash are these, at this time."
  - ContractRejection is the honest refusal, also signed.
  - EstablishedContract is the (offer, acceptance) pair. Verifies
    both signatures, that offer_hash and terms_hash match, and
    that the two worlds differ.
  - BilateralRevocation is both parties signing the same payload.
  - ContractRegistry is LOCAL state on each negotiator's side.
    It is not a WCP world, not shared. Each party keeps its own.

Composition:
  - Contract signatures verify against the same public keys that
    verify CuratorMessages (C55). A world's key is its voice.
  - Residents (C1 identities) cite contract_id in acts. The world
    kernel does NOT check the citation. The contract is a social
    artifact: residents honor it or don't, by verifying against
    their curators' registries.

House rules honored:
  - "Every behaviour has a test that fails if the behaviour
    breaks" — one per: offer signed, acceptance signed, rejection
    signed, mismatch rejected, established verified, revocation
    bilateral, one-sided revocation rejected, never raises.
  - "A world never raises on what a visitor sends" — receive
    methods return Ack/Refusal; verifiers return verdicts.
  - "History, not rank" — the registry is a record.

Honest limits (documented, tested):
  - No enforcement. The world kernel does not know about
    contracts. Residents cite; other residents check.
  - No timeout on offers. Offers persist until accepted,
    rejected, superseded by a newer offer from the same proposer
    to the same target, or revoked.
  - No arbitration. If two residents disagree about whether a
    citation is valid, there is no arbiter.
  - Contract ID = terms_hash means identical-terms offers from
    different proposers collide. Deliberate: same terms = same
    contract. A future component could add a nonce for uniqueness.
  - No sub-contracts (contracts referencing contracts).
"""

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from multiverse_c3 import Act, Ack, Refusal
from multiverse_c13 import (
    HAS_CRYPTO, KeyPair, canonical_bytes, verify_signature,
)
from multiverse_c55 import WorldCurator


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _hash_payload(p: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p).hexdigest()


# =====================================================================
# ContractTerms
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractTerms:
    """Free-form terms, hashable. Two offers with the same terms
    have the same terms_hash → the same contract ID."""
    content: Dict

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.content, dict):
            raise ValueError("terms content must be a dict")

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "contract_terms",
            "content": self.content,
        })

    def terms_hash(self) -> str:
        return _hash_payload(self.canonical_payload())

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "content": self.content,
            "terms_hash": self.terms_hash(),
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "ContractTerms":
        return cls(content=d["content"])


# =====================================================================
# ContractOffer
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractOffer:
    proposer_world_id: str
    proposer_public_key: str
    target_world_id: str
    terms: ContractTerms
    timestamp: str
    signature: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        for f in ("proposer_world_id", "target_world_id",
                  "timestamp", "signature"):
            v = getattr(self, f)
            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v:
                raise ValueError(f"{f} required")
        if len(self.proposer_public_key) != 64:
            raise ValueError(
                "proposer_public_key must be 64 hex chars")
        if self.proposer_world_id == self.target_world_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "cannot propose a contract to oneself")
        if not isinstance(self.terms, ContractTerms):
            raise ValueError("terms must be ContractTerms")

    @property
    def terms_hash(self) -> str:
        return self.terms.terms_hash()

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "contract_offer",
            "proposer_world_id": self.proposer_world_id,
            "proposer_public_key": self.proposer_public_key,
            "target_world_id": self.target_world_id,
            "terms": self.terms.content,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        })

    def offer_hash(self) -> str:
        return _hash_payload(self.canonical_payload())

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "proposer_world_id": self.proposer_world_id,
            "proposer_public_key": self.proposer_public_key,
            "target_world_id": self.target_world_id,
            "terms": self.terms.content,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "signature": self.signature,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "ContractOffer":
        return cls(
            proposer_world_id=d["proposer_world_id"],
            proposer_public_key=d["proposer_public_key"],
            target_world_id=d["target_world_id"],
            terms=ContractTerms(content=d["terms"]),
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )


def verify_contract_offer(
    offer: ContractOffer,
    expected_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        key = expected_public_key or offer.proposer_public_key
        return verify_signature(
            key, offer.canonical_payload(), offer.signature)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# ContractAcceptance
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractAcceptance:
    acceptor_world_id: str
    acceptor_public_key: str
    offer_hash: str
    terms_hash: str
    timestamp: str
    signature: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        for f in ("acceptor_world_id", "offer_hash",
                  "terms_hash", "timestamp", "signature"):
            v = getattr(self, f)
            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v:
                raise ValueError(f"{f} required")
        if len(self.acceptor_public_key) != 64:
            raise ValueError(
                "acceptor_public_key must be 64 hex chars")
        if len(self.offer_hash) != 64:
            raise ValueError("offer_hash must be 64 hex chars")
        if len(self.terms_hash) != 64:
            raise ValueError("terms_hash must be 64 hex chars")

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "contract_acceptance",
            "acceptor_world_id": self.acceptor_world_id,
            "acceptor_public_key": self.acceptor_public_key,
            "offer_hash": self.offer_hash,
            "terms_hash": self.terms_hash,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        })

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "acceptor_world_id": self.acceptor_world_id,
            "acceptor_public_key": self.acceptor_public_key,
            "offer_hash": self.offer_hash,
            "terms_hash": self.terms_hash,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "signature": self.signature,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "ContractAcceptance":
        return cls(
            acceptor_world_id=d["acceptor_world_id"],
            acceptor_public_key=d["acceptor_public_key"],
            offer_hash=d["offer_hash"],
            terms_hash=d["terms_hash"],
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )


def verify_contract_acceptance(
    acceptance: ContractAcceptance,
    expected_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        key = (expected_public_key
                or acceptance.acceptor_public_key)
        return verify_signature(
            key, acceptance.canonical_payload(),
            acceptance.signature)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# ContractRejection
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ContractRejection:
    rejector_world_id: str
    rejector_public_key: str
    offer_hash: str
    reason: str
    timestamp: str
    signature: str

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "contract_rejection",
            "rejector_world_id": self.rejector_world_id,
            "rejector_public_key": self.rejector_public_key,
            "offer_hash": self.offer_hash,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        })

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "rejector_world_id": self.rejector_world_id,
            "rejector_public_key": self.rejector_public_key,
            "offer_hash": self.offer_hash,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "signature": self.signature,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "ContractRejection":
        return cls(
            rejector_world_id=d["rejector_world_id"],
            rejector_public_key=d["rejector_public_key"],
            offer_hash=d["offer_hash"],
            reason=d.get("reason", ""),
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )


def verify_contract_rejection(
    rejection: ContractRejection,
    expected_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        key = (expected_public_key
                or rejection.rejector_public_key)
        return verify_signature(
            key, rejection.canonical_payload(),
            rejection.signature)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# EstablishedContract
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EstablishedContract:
    offer: ContractOffer
    acceptance: ContractAcceptance
    established_at: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not isinstance(self.offer, ContractOffer):
            raise ValueError("offer must be ContractOffer")
        if not isinstance(self.acceptance, ContractAcceptance):
            raise ValueError(
                "acceptance must be ContractAcceptance")

    @property
    def terms_hash(self) -> str:
        return self.offer.terms_hash

    @property
    def world_a_id(self) -> str:
        return self.offer.proposer_world_id

    @property
    def world_b_id(self) -> str:
        return self.offer.target_world_id

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "offer": self.offer.to_dict(),
            "acceptance": self.acceptance.to_dict(),
            "established_at": self.established_at,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "EstablishedContract":
        return cls(
            offer=ContractOffer.from_dict(d["offer"]),
            acceptance=ContractAcceptance.from_dict(
                d["acceptance"]),
            established_at=d["established_at"],
        )


def verify_established_contract(
    contract: EstablishedContract,
    proposer_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
    acceptor_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Verify an EstablishedContract. Never raises.

    Checks:
      1. Offer signature verifies.
      2. Acceptance signature verifies.
      3. Acceptance references this offer's hash.
      4. Acceptance references this offer's terms hash.
      5. Proposer world != acceptor world.
      6. Acceptance's acceptor world matches the offer's target.
    """
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return (False, "cryptography not installed")
    if not isinstance(contract, EstablishedContract):
        return (False, "not an EstablishedContract")

    # 1. Offer
    if not verify_contract_offer(
            contract.offer, proposer_public_key):
        return (False, "offer signature INVALID")

    # 2. Acceptance
    if not verify_contract_acceptance(
            contract.acceptance, acceptor_public_key):
        return (False, "acceptance signature INVALID")

    # 3. Offer hash match
    if contract.acceptance.offer_hash != \
            contract.offer.offer_hash():
        return (False, "acceptance references a different offer")

    # 4. Terms hash match
    if contract.acceptance.terms_hash != \
            contract.offer.terms_hash:
        return (False, "acceptance references different terms")

    # 5. Distinct worlds
    if contract.world_a_id == contract.world_b_id:
        return (False, "proposer and acceptor are the same world")

    # 6. Acceptor matches target
    if contract.acceptance.acceptor_world_id != \
            contract.offer.target_world_id:
        return (False,
                "acceptor is not the offer's target")

    return (True, "offer and acceptance verify; "
                   "hashes and worlds match")


# =====================================================================
# BilateralRevocation
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BilateralRevocation:
    contract_id: str
    world_a_id: str
    world_a_public_key: str
    world_b_id: str
    world_b_public_key: str
    reason: str
    timestamp: str
    signature_a: str
    signature_b: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        for f in ("contract_id", "world_a_id", "world_b_id",
                  "timestamp", "signature_a", "signature_b"):
            v = getattr(self, f)
            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v:
                raise ValueError(f"{f} required")
        for f in ("world_a_public_key", "world_b_public_key",
                  "contract_id"):
            if len(getattr(self, f)) != 64:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{f} must be 64 hex chars")
        if self.world_a_id == self.world_b_id:
            raise ValueError(
                "revocation requires two distinct worlds")

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "bilateral_revocation",
            "contract_id": self.contract_id,
            "world_a_id": self.world_a_id,
            "world_a_public_key": self.world_a_public_key,
            "world_b_id": self.world_b_id,
            "world_b_public_key": self.world_b_public_key,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        })

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "contract_id": self.contract_id,
            "world_a_id": self.world_a_id,
            "world_a_public_key": self.world_a_public_key,
            "world_b_id": self.world_b_id,
            "world_b_public_key": self.world_b_public_key,
            "reason": self.reason,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "signature_a": self.signature_a,
            "signature_b": self.signature_b,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "BilateralRevocation":
        return cls(
            contract_id=d["contract_id"],
            world_a_id=d["world_a_id"],
            world_a_public_key=d["world_a_public_key"],
            world_b_id=d["world_b_id"],
            world_b_public_key=d["world_b_public_key"],
            reason=d.get("reason", ""),
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signature_a=d["signature_a"],
            signature_b=d["signature_b"],
        )


def verify_bilateral_revocation(
    revocation: BilateralRevocation,
    world_a_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
    world_b_public_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Verify a BilateralRevocation. Never raises.

    Both signatures must be present and valid.
    """
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return (False, "cryptography not installed")
    if not isinstance(revocation, BilateralRevocation):
        return (False, "not a BilateralRevocation")
    key_a = world_a_public_key or revocation.world_a_public_key
    key_b = world_b_public_key or revocation.world_b_public_key
    payload = revocation.canonical_payload()
    try:
        sig_a_ok = verify_signature(
            key_a, payload, revocation.signature_a)
    except Exception:
        sig_a_ok = False
    try:
        sig_b_ok = verify_signature(
            key_b, payload, revocation.signature_b)
    except Exception:
        sig_b_ok = False
    if not sig_a_ok and not sig_b_ok:
        return (False, "both signatures INVALID")
    if not sig_a_ok:
        return (False, "world_a signature INVALID")
    if not sig_b_ok:
        return (False, "world_b signature INVALID")
    return (True, "both signatures valid")

def sign_offer(
    proposer_world_id: str,
    proposer_kp: KeyPair,
    target_world_id: str,
    terms: ContractTerms,
    timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
) -> ContractOffer:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("sign_offer requires cryptography")
    if timestamp is None:
        timestamp = _now()
    payload = canonical_bytes({
        "kind": "contract_offer",
        "proposer_world_id": proposer_world_id,
        "proposer_public_key": proposer_kp.public_key_hex(),
        "target_world_id": target_world_id,
        "terms": terms.content,
        "timestamp": timestamp,
    })
    return ContractOffer(
        proposer_world_id=proposer_world_id,
        proposer_public_key=proposer_kp.public_key_hex(),
        target_world_id=target_world_id,
        terms=terms,
        timestamp=timestamp,
        signature=proposer_kp.sign(payload).hex(),
    )


def sign_acceptance(
    acceptor_world_id: str,
    acceptor_kp: KeyPair,
    offer: ContractOffer,
    timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
) -> ContractAcceptance:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "sign_acceptance requires cryptography")
    if timestamp is None:
        timestamp = _now()
    payload = canonical_bytes({
        "kind": "contract_acceptance",
        "acceptor_world_id": acceptor_world_id,
        "acceptor_public_key": acceptor_kp.public_key_hex(),
        "offer_hash": offer.offer_hash(),
        "terms_hash": offer.terms_hash,
        "timestamp": timestamp,
    })
    return ContractAcceptance(
        acceptor_world_id=acceptor_world_id,
        acceptor_public_key=acceptor_kp.public_key_hex(),
        offer_hash=offer.offer_hash(),
        terms_hash=offer.terms_hash,
        timestamp=timestamp,
        signature=acceptor_kp.sign(payload).hex(),
    )

# =====================================================================
# ContractRegistry
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class ContractRecord:
    terms_hash: str
    world_a_id: str
    world_b_id: str
    offer: Optional[ContractOffer] = None
    acceptance: Optional[ContractAcceptance] = None
    rejection: Optional[ContractRejection] = None
    revocation: Optional[BilateralRevocation] = None
    established_at: Optional[str] = None
    revoked_at: Optional[str] = None

    def is_established(self) -> bool:
        return (self.offer is not None
                and self.acceptance is not None
                and self.revocation is None)

    def is_rejected(self) -> bool:
        return (self.rejection is not None
                and self.acceptance is None)

    def is_revoked(self) -> bool:
        return self.revocation is not None

    def is_pending(self) -> bool:
        return (self.offer is not None
                and self.acceptance is None
                and self.rejection is None)

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "terms_hash": self.terms_hash,
            "world_a_id": self.world_a_id,
            "world_b_id": self.world_b_id,
            "offer": self.offer.to_dict() if self.offer else None,
            "acceptance":
                self.acceptance.to_dict()
                if self.acceptance else None,
            "rejection":
                self.rejection.to_dict()
                if self.rejection else None,
            "revocation":
                self.revocation.to_dict()
                if self.revocation else None,
            "established_at": self.established_at,
            "revoked_at": self.revoked_at,
        }


class ContractRegistry:
    """Local, per-world registry of contract artifacts.

    Each curator/negotiator has its own. There is no shared state.
    A contract is "established" from this registry's perspective
    when both offer and acceptance have been seen.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._records: Dict[str, ContractRecord] = {}

    def _get_or_create(
        self, terms_hash: str,
        world_a_id: str, world_b_id: str,
    ) -> ContractRecord:
        if terms_hash not in self._records:
            self._records[terms_hash] = ContractRecord(
                terms_hash=terms_hash,
                world_a_id=world_a_id,
                world_b_id=world_b_id,
            )
        return self._records[terms_hash]

    def register_offer(self, offer: ContractOffer) -> None:
        rec = self._get_or_create(
            offer.terms_hash,
            offer.proposer_world_id,
            offer.target_world_id)
        rec.offer = offer

    def register_acceptance(
        self, acceptance: ContractAcceptance,
    ) -> None:
        # Acceptance doesn't carry world_a_id / world_b_id; the
        # offer must already be present (or the terms_hash won't
        # match anything in the registry — the caller should have
        # registered the offer first).
        for rec in self._records.values():
            if rec.terms_hash == acceptance.terms_hash:
                rec.acceptance = acceptance
                rec.established_at = _now()
                return
        # Acceptance without matching offer — record under a
        # partially-known record
        rec = self._get_or_create(
            acceptance.terms_hash,
            world_a_id="?",
            world_b_id=acceptance.acceptor_world_id)
        rec.acceptance = acceptance
        rec.established_at = _now()

    def register_rejection(
        self, rejection: ContractRejection,
    ) -> None:
        # Find by offer hash
        for rec in self._records.values():
            if rec.offer is not None and \
                    rec.offer.offer_hash() == rejection.offer_hash:
                rec.rejection = rejection
                return
        # No matching record; ignore (rejection of unknown offer)

    def register_revocation(
        self, revocation: BilateralRevocation,
    ) -> None:
        rec = self._records.get(revocation.contract_id)
        if rec is None:
            rec = self._get_or_create(
                revocation.contract_id,
                revocation.world_a_id,
                revocation.world_b_id)
        rec.revocation = revocation
        rec.revoked_at = _now()

    def get(self, terms_hash: str) -> Optional[ContractRecord]:
        return self._records.get(terms_hash)

    def list_all(self) -> List[ContractRecord]:
        return list(self._records.values())

    def established(self) -> List[ContractRecord]:
        return [r for r in self._records.values()
                if r.is_established()]

    def pending(self) -> List[ContractRecord]:
        return [r for r in self._records.values()
                if r.is_pending()]

    def revoked(self) -> List[ContractRecord]:
        return [r for r in self._records.values()
                if r.is_revoked()]

    def is_active(self, terms_hash: str) -> bool:
        rec = self._records.get(terms_hash)
        if rec is None:
            return False
        return rec.is_established()


# =====================================================================
# ContractNegotiator — the integration with C55's curator
# =====================================================================

class ContractNegotiator:
    """A negotiator wrapping a WorldCurator. Provides the contract
    negotiation API on top of C55's curator. C55 is untouched.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        curator: WorldCurator,
        registry: Optional[ContractRegistry] = None,
    ):
        self._curator = curator
        self._registry = registry or ContractRegistry()

    @property
    def world_id(self) -> str:
        return self._curator.world_id

    @property
    def public_key(self) -> str:
        return self._curator.public_key

    @property
    def curator(self) -> WorldCurator:
        return self._curator

    @property
    def registry(self) -> ContractRegistry:
        return self._registry

    def propose(
        self, target_world_id: str, terms: ContractTerms,
    ) -> ContractOffer:
        """Propose a contract. Registers the offer locally."""
        offer = sign_offer(
            self.world_id, self._curator._world_kp,
            target_world_id, terms)
        self._registry.register_offer(offer)
        return offer

    def receive_offer(self, offer: ContractOffer):
        """Receive a contract offer addressed to us. Verifies the
        signature and target; registers if valid."""
        if not isinstance(offer, ContractOffer):
            return Refusal(reason="not a ContractOffer")
        if not verify_contract_offer(offer):
            return Refusal(reason="offer signature INVALID")
        if offer.target_world_id != self.world_id:
            return Refusal(
                reason="offer not addressed to this world")
        self._registry.register_offer(offer)
        return Ack(
            entity_id=self.world_id, timestamp=_now())

    def accept(
        self, offer: ContractOffer,
    ) -> ContractAcceptance:
        """Accept an offer. Registers the acceptance locally."""
        acceptance = sign_acceptance(
            self.world_id, self._curator._world_kp, offer)
        self._registry.register_offer(offer)
        self._registry.register_acceptance(acceptance)
        return acceptance

    def reject(
        self, offer: ContractOffer, reason: str = "",
    ) -> ContractRejection:
        rejection = sign_rejection(
            self.world_id, self._curator._world_kp,
            offer, reason)
        self._registry.register_offer(offer)
        self._registry.register_rejection(rejection)
        return rejection

    def receive_acceptance(
        self, acceptance: ContractAcceptance,
    ):
        """Receive an acceptance for one of our offers. Verifies
        the signature; registers if valid."""
        if not isinstance(acceptance, ContractAcceptance):
            return Refusal(reason="not a ContractAcceptance")
        if not verify_contract_acceptance(acceptance):
            return Refusal(reason="acceptance signature INVALID")
        self._registry.register_acceptance(acceptance)
        return Ack(
            entity_id=self.world_id, timestamp=_now())

    def receive_rejection(
        self, rejection: ContractRejection,
    ):
        if not isinstance(rejection, ContractRejection):
            return Refusal(reason="not a ContractRejection")
        if not verify_contract_rejection(rejection):
            return Refusal(reason="rejection signature INVALID")
        self._registry.register_rejection(rejection)
        return Ack(
            entity_id=self.world_id, timestamp=_now())

    def is_active(self, terms_hash: str) -> bool:
        """True iff this world has an established, non-revoked
        contract with the given terms hash."""
        return self._registry.is_active(terms_hash)

    def get_contract(
        self, terms_hash: str,
    ) -> Optional[ContractRecord]:
        return self._registry.get(terms_hash)
```

Demo

```python
def demo(artifact_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
    """Two worlds negotiate a contract, a resident cites it, and
    the contract is later revoked bilaterally.

    Scenario A: happy path
      1. Curators A and B (C55) establish a link.
      2. A proposes a mutual-recognition contract.
      3. B receives, accepts.
      4. A receives the acceptance. Both registries show the
         contract as established.
      5. A resident of A submits an act to B citing the contract.
      6. B's negotiator confirms the contract is active.

    Scenario B: tampered offer
      Attacker flips a term in the offer. Verification fails.

    Scenario C: mismatched acceptance
      Acceptance references a different offer. The assembled
      EstablishedContract fails verification.

    Scenario D: one-sided revocation
      A signs a revocation but B doesn't. Verification fails.

    Anchor: Dickinson, 'I'm Nobody! Who are you?'
    (contract between strangers who agree to recognize each other).
    """
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    from multiverse_c3 import Act
    from multiverse_c4 import PoetryWorld
    from multiverse_c5 import ChemistryWorld

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")

    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir)
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Two worlds and their curators
    world_a = PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "Poetry")
    world_b = ChemistryWorld("world:chemistry", "Chemistry")
    kp_a = KeyPair.generate()
    kp_b = KeyPair.generate()
    curator_a = WorldCurator(world_a, kp_a)
    curator_b = WorldCurator(world_b, kp_b)

    # C55 link first (contracts and links are independent, but
    # a link is a reasonable precondition for negotiating)
    req = curator_a.request_link(curator_b.world_id)
    curator_b.receive(req)
    curator_b.respond_hello(req)
    ack_a, _ = curator_a.respond_hello(req)

    neg_a = ContractNegotiator(curator_a)
    neg_b = ContractNegotiator(curator_b)

    # -- Scenario A: happy path -------------------------------
    terms = ContractTerms(content={
        "kind": "mutual-recognition",
        "poetry_accepts": "chem-element-rulings",
        "chemistry_accepts": "poetry-stanza-rulings",
        "scope": "cross-world-act-validation",
    })
    offer = neg_a.propose(neg_b.world_id, terms)

    ack_offer = neg_b.receive_offer(offer)
    assert isinstance(ack_offer, Ack)
    acceptance = neg_b.accept(offer)

    ack_acc = neg_a.receive_acceptance(acceptance)
    assert isinstance(ack_acc, Ack)

    contract = EstablishedContract(
        offer=offer,
        acceptance=acceptance,
        established_at=_now(),
    )
    ok_happy, reason_happy = verify_established_contract(
        contract, kp_a.public_key_hex(), kp_b.public_key_hex())
    contract_id = terms.terms_hash()

    # Resident of A cites the contract in an act submitted to B.
    # The world kernel records the citation; the negotiator on
    # B's side can confirm it's still valid.
    resident_act = Act(
        actor_token="alice:token",
        type="poetry.turn",
        payload={
            "acknowledgment": "seed",
            "proposal": "a poem line",
            "invitation": "what next?",
            "holds_open": True,
            "cites_contract": contract_id,
        })
    # B's world would receive this; we just demonstrate that the
    # negotiator on either side can confirm the contract is active.
    active_from_b = neg_b.is_active(contract_id)
    active_from_a = neg_a.is_active(contract_id)

    # -- Scenario B: tampered offer ---------------------------
    # Flip one term
    tampered_terms = ContractTerms(content={
        **terms.content,
        "poetry_accepts": "TAMPERED",
    })
    tampered_offer = ContractOffer(
        proposer_world_id=offer.proposer_world_id,
        proposer_public_key=offer.proposer_public_key,
        target_world_id=offer.target_world_id,
        terms=tampered_terms,
        timestamp=offer.timestamp,
        signature=offer.signature,  # old sig
    )
    ok_tamper, reason_tamper = verify_established_contract(
        EstablishedContract(
            offer=tampered_offer,
            acceptance=acceptance,
            established_at=_now()),
        kp_a.public_key_hex(), kp_b.public_key_hex())

    # -- Scenario C: mismatched acceptance -------------------
    # Acceptance references a different offer hash
    bad_acceptance = ContractAcceptance(
        acceptor_world_id=acceptance.acceptor_world_id,
        acceptor_public_key=acceptance.acceptor_public_key,
        offer_hash="ff" * 32,  # wrong
        terms_hash=acceptance.terms_hash,
        timestamp=acceptance.timestamp,
        signature=acceptance.signature)
    ok_mismatch, reason_mismatch = verify_established_contract(
        EstablishedContract(
            offer=offer,
            acceptance=bad_acceptance,
            established_at=_now()),
        kp_a.public_key_hex(), kp_b.public_key_hex())

    # -- Scenario D: one-sided revocation --------------------
    # A signs, B doesn't (only one sig)
    rev = sign_bilateral_revocation(
        contract_id=contract_id,
        world_a_id=neg_a.world_id,
        world_a_kp=kp_a,
        world_b_id=neg_b.world_id,
        world_b_kp=kp_b,
        reason="test revocation",
    )
    # Now forge a one-sided version
    attacker = KeyPair.generate()
    one_sided = BilateralRevocation(
        contract_id=rev.contract_id,
        world_a_id=rev.world_a_id,
        world_a_public_key=rev.world_a_public_key,
        world_b_id=rev.world_b_id,
        world_b_public_key=rev.world_b_public_key,
        reason=rev.reason,
        timestamp=rev.timestamp,
        signature_a=rev.signature_a,
        signature_b=attacker.sign(rev.canonical_payload()).hex())
    ok_oneside, reason_oneside = verify_bilateral_revocation(
        one_sided, kp_a.public_key_hex(),
        kp_b.public_key_hex())

    # -- Print -----------------------------------------------
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Curator-Mediated Contract — two worlds agree")
    print("=" * 70)
    print()
    print(f"  World A: {neg_a.world_id}")
    print(f"  World B: {neg_b.world_id}")
    print(f"  Terms:   {terms.content.get('kind')}")
    print(f"  Contract ID: {contract_id[:16]}...")
    print()
    print("  Scenario A: happy path")
    print(f"    Offer signed by A:       True")
    print(f"    Acceptance signed by B:  True")
    print(f"    Established contract:    "
          f"{'✓' if ok_happy else '✗'} ({reason_happy})")
    print(f"    Active on A's side:      {active_from_a}")
    print(f"    Active on B's side:      {active_from_b}")
    print()
    print("  Scenario B: tampered terms in the offer")
    print(f"    Verification: {'✓' if ok_tamper else '✗'} "
          f"({reason_tamper})")
    print()
    print("  Scenario C: acceptance references a different offer")
    print(f"    Verification: {'✓' if ok_mismatch else '✗'} "
          f"({reason_mismatch})")
    print()
    print("  Scenario D: one-sided revocation")
    print(f"    Verification: {'✓' if ok_oneside else '✗'} "
          f"({reason_oneside})")
    print()
    print("  What this demonstrates:")
    print("    - A contract is a pattern of signed artifacts.")
    print("    - Both signatures verify against world public keys.")
    print("    - The contract ID is the terms hash: same terms")
    print("      = same contract, on any two worlds.")
    print("    - Residents cite the contract; readers verify")
    print("      against their curators' registries.")
    print("    - The world kernel does not enforce contracts.")
    print("      That's the honest architecture: verification,")
    print("      not enforcement.")
    print("    - No new primitive. C1, C13, C55, C57 compose.")
    print()
    print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
    print("    'I'm Nobody! Who are you?'")
    print("    'Are you – Nobody – too?'")

    audit = {
        "world_a": neg_a.world_id,
        "world_b": neg_b.world_id,
        "contract_id": contract_id,
        "terms": terms.content,
        "happy_path": {
            "established": ok_happy,
            "reason": reason_happy,
            "active_from_a": active_from_a,
            "active_from_b": active_from_b,
        },
        "tampered_offer": {
            "verified": ok_tamper,
            "reason": reason_tamper,
        },
        "mismatched_acceptance": {
            "verified": ok_mismatch,
            "reason": reason_mismatch,
        },
        "one_sided_revocation": {
            "verified": ok_oneside,
            "reason": reason_oneside,
        },
    }
    (path / "contract_demo.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
    print(f"\n  → {path}/contract_demo.json")
    return audit
```

    not HAS_CRYPTO, reason="cryptography not installed")


# =====================================================================
# Helpers

def _make_pair(name_a="a", name_b="b"):
    from multiverse_c4 import PoetryWorld
    from multiverse_c5 import ChemistryWorld
    world_a = PoetryWorld(f"world:{name_a}", name_a)
    world_b = ChemistryWorld(f"world:{name_b}", name_b)
    kp_a = KeyPair.generate()
    kp_b = KeyPair.generate()
    curator_a = WorldCurator(world_a, kp_a)
    curator_b = WorldCurator(world_b, kp_b)
    return {
        "world_a": world_a, "world_b": world_b,
        "kp_a": kp_a, "kp_b": kp_b,
        "curator_a": curator_a, "curator_b": curator_b,
        "neg_a": ContractNegotiator(curator_a),
        "neg_b": ContractNegotiator(curator_b),
    }


def _make_terms(**overrides):
    base = {"kind": "test", "clause": "x"}
    base.update(overrides)
    return ContractTerms(content=base)


# =====================================================================
# ContractTerms
# =====================================================================

def test_terms_validates_content():
    print("=== ContractTerms: content must be dict ===")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ContractTerms(content="not a dict")


def test_terms_hash_deterministic():
    print("=== ContractTerms: hash is deterministic ===")
    t1 = ContractTerms(content={"a": 1, "b": 2})
    t2 = ContractTerms(content={"b": 2, "a": 1})
    assert t1.terms_hash() == t2.terms_hash()


def test_terms_hash_differs_on_content():
    print("=== ContractTerms: different content → different hash ===")
    t1 = ContractTerms(content={"a": 1})
    t2 = ContractTerms(content={"a": 2})
    assert t1.terms_hash() != t2.terms_hash()


# =====================================================================
# Sign / verify offer
# =====================================================================

def test_offer_signed_by_proposer():
    print("=== Offer: signed by proposer's key ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    terms = _make_terms()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id,
        parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id,
        terms)
    assert verify_contract_offer(
        offer, parts["kp_a"].public_key_hex())


def test_offer_wrong_key():
    print("=== Offer: wrong key → False ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, _make_terms())
    wrong = KeyPair.generate()
    assert not verify_contract_offer(
        offer, wrong.public_key_hex())


def test_offer_rejects_self_target():
    print("=== Offer: rejects proposing to oneself ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        sign_offer(
            parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
            parts["neg_a"].world_id, _make_terms())


def test_offer_rejects_empty_fields():
    print("=== ContractOffer: validates fields ===")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ContractOffer(
            proposer_world_id="",
            proposer_public_key="aa" * 32,
            target_world_id="b",
            terms=_make_terms(),
            timestamp="t", signature="s")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ContractOffer(
            proposer_world_id="a",
            proposer_public_key="short",
            target_world_id="b",
            terms=_make_terms(),
            timestamp="t", signature="s")

def test_established_contract_bad_offer_sig():
    print("=== EstablishedContract: bad offer signature ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, _make_terms())
    acc = sign_acceptance(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, parts["kp_b"], offer)
    # Tamper with offer signature
    attacker = KeyPair.generate()
    tampered_offer = ContractOffer(
        proposer_world_id=offer.proposer_world_id,
        proposer_public_key=offer.proposer_public_key,
        target_world_id=offer.target_world_id,
        terms=offer.terms,
        timestamp=offer.timestamp,
        signature=attacker.sign(
            offer.canonical_payload()).hex())
    contract = EstablishedContract(
        offer=tampered_offer, acceptance=acc,
        established_at=_now())
    ok, reason = verify_established_contract(
        contract,
        parts["kp_a"].public_key_hex(),
        parts["kp_b"].public_key_hex())
    assert not ok
    assert "offer" in reason.lower()

def test_negotiator_propose():

    assert rec.is_pending()

    assert isinstance(r, Refusal)

    print("=== Negotiator.receive_offer: bad sig → Refusal ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, _make_terms())
    attacker = KeyPair.generate()
    tampered = ContractOffer(

        proposer_public_key=offer.proposer_public_key,
        target_world_id=offer.target_world_id,

    r = parts["neg_b"].receive_offer(tampered)
    assert isinstance(r, Refusal)


def test_negotiator_full_flow():
    print("=== Negotiator: full flow (offer → accept → established) ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    terms = _make_terms()
    offer = parts["neg_a"].propose(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, terms)
    ack = parts["neg_b"].receive_offer(offer)
    assert isinstance(ack, Ack)
    acc = parts["neg_b"].accept(offer)
    ack2 = parts["neg_a"].receive_acceptance(acc)
    assert isinstance(ack2, Ack)
    # Both sides see the contract as established
    assert parts["neg_a"].is_active(terms.terms_hash())
    assert parts["neg_b"].is_active(terms.terms_hash())


def test_negotiator_reject():
    print("=== Negotiator: reject ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    terms = _make_terms()
    offer = parts["neg_a"].propose(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, terms)
    parts["neg_b"].receive_offer(offer)
    rej = parts["neg_b"].reject(offer, reason="bad terms")
    # A receives the rejection
    ack = parts["neg_a"].receive_rejection(rej)
    assert isinstance(ack, Ack)
    rec = parts["neg_a"].get_contract(terms.terms_hash())
    assert rec.is_rejected()
    assert not rec.is_established()


def test_negotiator_revocation_via_registry():
    print("=== Negotiator: bilateral revocation via registry ===")
    parts = _make_pair()
    terms = _make_terms()
    offer = parts["neg_a"].propose(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, terms)
    acc = parts["neg_b"].accept(offer)
    parts["neg_a"].receive_acceptance(acc)
    assert parts["neg_a"].is_active(terms.terms_hash())
    # Bilateral revocation
    rev = sign_bilateral_revocation(
        contract_id=terms.terms_hash(),
        world_a_id=parts["neg_a"].world_id,
        world_a_kp=parts["kp_a"],
        world_b_id=parts["neg_b"].world_id,
        world_b_kp=parts["kp_b"],
        reason="revoked by mutual agreement")
    parts["neg_a"].registry.register_revocation(rev)
    parts["neg_b"].registry.register_revocation(rev)
    assert not parts["neg_a"].is_active(terms.terms_hash())
    assert not parts["neg_b"].is_active(terms.terms_hash())

def test_registry_pending():
    print("=== Registry: pending ===")
    reg = ContractRegistry()
    parts = _make_pair()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, _make_terms())
    reg.register_offer(offer)
    assert len(reg.pending()) == 1
    assert len(reg.established()) == 0


def test_registry_established():
    print("=== Registry: established ===")
    reg = ContractRegistry()
    parts = _make_pair()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, _make_terms())
    acc = sign_acceptance(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, parts["kp_b"], offer)
    reg.register_offer(offer)
    reg.register_acceptance(acc)
    assert len(reg.established()) == 1
    assert len(reg.pending()) == 0


def test_registry_revoked():
    print("=== Registry: revoked ===")
    reg = ContractRegistry()
    parts = _make_pair()
    terms = _make_terms()
    offer = sign_offer(
        parts["neg_a"].world_id, parts["kp_a"],
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, terms)
    acc = sign_acceptance(
        parts["neg_b"].world_id, parts["kp_b"], offer)
    reg.register_offer(offer)
    reg.register_acceptance(acc)
    rev = sign_bilateral_revocation(
        contract_id=terms.terms_hash(),
        world_a_id=parts["neg_a"].world_id,
        world_a_kp=parts["kp_a"],
        world_b_id=parts["neg_b"].world_id,
        world_b_kp=parts["kp_b"])
    reg.register_revocation(rev)
    assert len(reg.revoked()) == 1
    assert not reg.is_active(terms.terms_hash())

def test_negotiator_is_not_a_world():
    print("=== Negotiator: is not a WCP world ===")

    assert not hasattr(parts["neg_a"], "manifest")
    assert not hasattr(parts["neg_a"], "petition")
    # But has negotiation methods

    assert hasattr(parts["neg_a"], "accept")
    assert hasattr(parts["neg_a"], "reject")
